data.title: Show HN: We're two coffee nerds who built an AI app to track beans and recipes
data.author: rokeyzhang
data.article_summary: BeanBook AI是一款专为咖啡爱好者设计的应用程序，可通过拍照或输入URL帮助用户追踪咖啡豆和食谱。用户可以将自己收藏的咖啡豆建立数字档案，将杂乱的抽屉变成有序的咖啡架。同时，应用可以将YouTube、博客或Reddit上的内容 instantaneously 转换为分步冲煮指南，并保存手写笔记。BeanBook AI还提供自动生成的年度咖啡回顾，包括统计数据和历史记录，并允许用户探索咖啡的风味、故事和背后的人文意义。该应用专为 specialty coffee 爱好者打造，兼具趣味性和实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一款新推出的咖啡日志应用的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• [质疑设计和情感表达的实际意义] spiralcoaster 对评论中提到的“从设计角度捕捉咖啡工具的情感”表示嘲讽，认为这种说法荒谬可笑，暗示这种表述过于主观和模糊。
• [与其他应用的对比] desigooner 对应用的独特性提出质疑，指出已有的开源应用 Beanconqueror 功能完善，且支持与硬件设备（如秤和折射计）的集成，询问新应用相比之下有何优势。
• [账户和隐私问题] whoamii 对应用仅接受 Google/Apple 账户登录表示不满，质疑为何必须创建账户，表达了对隐私和便利性的担忧。

补充讨论：
• [期待功能和使用体验] jeemusu 表示对应用的期待，尤其是希望看到其他用户的使用笔记，特别是使用相似设备的人，以帮助更快上手新豆子。同时提到对安卓版本的需求。
• [功能建议] tiltowait 建议应用增加根据用户拥有的设备提供定制化建议的功能，例如根据用户的磨豆机型号推荐具体的研磨设置。
• [设计反馈] ladidahh 对应用的设计表示赞赏，但认为宣传视频未能很好地展示应用的UI优点，建议改进视频以更好地展示应用的设计亮点。
• [个人经验分享] rorylaitila 祝贺应用发布并分享了自己曾经手动建立数据库跟踪烘焙和品尝笔记的经历，指出如果能有一个类似 Vivino 的应用来跟踪咖啡会很有趣。
• [对类似应用的需求] mastazi 作为咖啡爱好者，一直希望有一个类似 Vivino 的咖啡应用，对新应用的发布表示赞赏。
• [个人项目未完成的情感] wmrío 祝贺应用发布，同时表达了自己未完成类似项目的遗憾和羡慕。
• [具体功能需求] easygenes 对应用的烘焙选项提出了具体建议，希望能够更详细地输入烘焙数据，特别是从特定设备（如 DiFluid Omni）获取的数据。
• [热情支持] garysahota93 对应用表示强烈支持，希望与开发者交流更多想法和反馈。
• [快速支持和下载] wjgilmore 和 radicaldreamer 简单直接地表示了对应用的兴奋和支持，wjgilmore 还提到已经下载应用准备试用。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于应用的独特性和必要性，特别是与已有开源应用（如 Beanconqueror）的对比，以及账户要求的合理性。用户对是否真的需要另一个类似应用以及隐私问题表示关注。

data.title: People Keep Inventing Prolly Trees
data.author: lifty
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“多重发现”现象，即科学发现常由不同人在相近时间独立完成，例如牛顿和莱布尼茨同时发明微积分，以及达尔文和华莱士同时提出进化论。文章提出，多重发现可能是常态，发明常是社会条件的产物，当发现的前提条件成熟时，往往会迅速被多次发现。文章还以“概率树”（prolly trees）为例，说明这种数据结构在不同领域和名称下被独立发明了至少四次，显示其是既有概念的创新组合，而非全新创造。概率树结合了内容定义分块和Merkle树等已有技术，其发明是技术发展的自然结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据结构（尤其是Prolly Trees及其相关概念）的历史、应用、实现细节及相关争议

不同观点：
• wmanley认为Prolly Trees的概念并非新颖，早在2005和2009年就有类似的数据结构（如Merkle hash tree和rsync算法）被提出和讨论。他引用了Martin Uecker和C. Scott Ananian的邮件作为证据，表明这些概念在早期已经被探索过。
• gritzko指出Prolly Trees可以看作是Merkle-fied B-trees，并提到他正在研究相关的Merkle-fied LSM trees。他还提到许多数据结构的“发明”实际上是已有概念的改进，所有计算机科学的基础似乎早在70年代和80年代就已经被发明。
• compressedgas补充了Jumbostore（2007年）的例子，认为其使用的递归内容定义分块与Prolly Trees本质上是相同的。
• ChadNauseam讨论了滚动哈希分块与其加密应用的结合，提出了一种文件备份和 deduplication 的策略，并顺便提到下载大文件的体验问题。
• inetknght分享了个人经历，指出很多人可能没有意识到自己“发明”了新颖的数据结构，因为这些设计在他们看来是显而易见的。
• elric质疑如何有效地找到不熟悉但具有特定性质的数据结构，并询问是否存在基于属性的搜索方法。
• jerf欣赏数据结构的研究，认为学习数据结构能帮助理解和应用各种技巧，尽管现代计算机的快速发展使得一些复杂的数据结构变得不那么必要。
• donatj认为Prolly Trees缺乏足够的资料和普及，建议了解该结构的人为其创建维基百科页面。
• iamwil提出了关于编辑Prolly Trees时是否需要从叶子节点重新构建整个树的疑问，并表示自己实现了一种相关方法，询问是否对其他人有价值。
• guywithahat引用了一位前上司的话，认为研究通常比行业实践落后5-10年，Prolly Trees似乎也是如此。
• zombot对“概率平衡”这一术语表示困惑，希望得到解释。

补充讨论：
• 关于Prolly Trees的历史与类似概念的讨论，特别是它们是否为新颖的发明，还是对已有概念的改进。
• 关于数据结构的具体实现细节，例如编辑Prolly Trees时的重建问题。
• 对如何有效搜索和学习特定数据结构的需求和建议。
• 对Prolly Trees及其他相关数据结构的普及和资料不足的问题。
• 关于“概率平衡”术语的定义和理解的争议。

争议焦点：
• Prolly Trees是否为新颖的数据结构，还是对已有概念的重新发明和改进。
• 如何有效定义和理解“概率平衡”这一术语。

44407708.article_content:
Blog
Multiple Discovery
refers to when a scientific discovery is made independently by multiple individuals around the same time. The most well-known examples are Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz's independent invention of calculus, and Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace's independent formulation of the theory of evolution.
(Source:
https://xkcd.com/626/
)
There's even a hypothesis
1
that multiple discovery is the norm, rather than an exception: that invention is an result of social conditions rather than any single "great thinker", and that once the conditions for a discovery are met, that discovery is often made multiple times in rapid succession.
It's not always immediately obvious when multiple discovery happens. There's several reasons why a case of multiple discovery might go unnoticed:
New inventions may bring new terminology or be used in different fields for different purposes. It may require an intimate understanding of the field to even realize that these separate inventions are actually the same thing.
Sometimes an invention is not widely known because its creator doesn't realize they've created something novel: the design seemed obvious and intuitive to them.
But if we see multiple discovery happening, it's a strong indication that the thing being discovered is in enough demand that it's going to
keep
being discovered, at least until knowledge of it eventually becomes commonplace. And it won't stop being discovered even then:
calculus was still being discovered in 1994.
This is all relevant because of how it relates to one of our favorite data structures:
prolly trees
.
We talk about prolly trees a lot, because they're the novel tool that makes Dolt possible. We didn't invent them, we have
Noms
to thank for that. But we did see the value in using them to build the world's first version controlled relational database.
Except it turns out that Noms isn't the only group to invent prolly trees. Just like calculus, prolly trees have been independently invented at least four times now, under different names and used in different contexts. And I think that's worth a closer look.
2015: Noms Invents Prolly Trees
In 2015, Noms
coined the term "Prolly Tree"
for their tree data structure with the following really nice properties:
searchable
- They can store ordered data and perform lookups based on ordered keys or offsets.
history independence
-
Any data set has a unique representation, regardless of the sequence of operations that led to the current state.
self-balancing
- The tree is probabilistically balanced.
structural sharing
-
Storing multiple versions of the data only requires additional storage proportional to their diff: duplicate parts of the data are deduplicated.
efficient diffing
-
It's possible to compare two prolly trees (or two snapshots of the same prolly tree) and identify only the parts of the data that are different between the two trees.
The time complexity is logarithmic on the total data size, and is only linear on the size of the diff.
efficient mutation
- Applying changes to the data stored in a prolly tree produces a new prolly tree. Like with diffing, the time complexity is logarithmic on the total data size, and is only linear on the size of the diff.
These properties make prolly trees great whenever you need to version control structured data, or need to reconcile data changes that may be received out-of-order.
I genuinely think prolly trees are novel. But I also think that they're are a textbook example of something that seems like an natural next step once you understand the prior work that it's built on: the novelty isn't in creating something new, but in combining existing math in a novel way. A prolly tree is ultimately nothing more than a
Merkle Tree
built by recursively applying a
Content-Defined Chunker
, such as with a
rolling hash function
.
None of these concepts are new:
Content-Defined Chunking is a core part of
rsync
, which was first released in 1996, although the concept itself is even older.
The first rolling hash function, the
Rabin fingerprint
, was proposed in 1981.
Merkle trees were patented in 1979.
If you understand these individual concepts, it's easy to see how they can be combined to create a tree structure that has all of these properties. It just took a little while to reach a point where prolly trees were needed.
In fact, there's a lot of prior art of things that are
almost
prolly trees:
rsync
uses content-defined chunking to split large files, but stores the chunk hashes in a flat list instead of in a Merkle tree.
BitTorrent
magnet links represent the torrent data as a Merkle tree of chunks, but the chunks are fixed-size, not content-defined.
IPFS
uses content-defined chunking to split large files, and then represents these chunks as a Merkle tree, but because the content-defined chunking is not applied recursively, the inner nodes of the tree are prone to shift.

data.title: Bulk Lots of DB-19s for Sale
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Steve出售大量DB-19连接器的消息。DB-19连接器曾在1980年代的Apple II、Macintosh、Atari和NeXT电脑中使用，后因停产而稀缺。2016年，Steve委托工厂重新生产DB-19，以满足其BMOW Floppy Emu磁盘模拟器的需求，无意中成为最大库存持有者。2025年，他决定通过eBay拍卖出售这些连接器，每批1000个，起拍价为每个0.44美元。这些全新制造的DB-19连接器为全金属外壳，适用于多种 vintage 电脑项目。拍卖将于7月8日结束，不单独出售或小批量出售。感兴趣者可查看eBay链接参与竞拍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DB-19连接器的相关讨论，包括购买意愿、具体类型、市场价格以及背景信息

不同观点：
• [Suppafly] 认为，虽然某人愿意分享一部分连接器是好事，但大多数人可能只需要购买少量而不是1000个。这里表达了对实际需求量的不同看法，暗示1000个的数量可能过大。

• [nxobject] 指出，目前讨论的DB-19连接器仅适用于男性DB-19（即用于外设），而对于女性DB-19（如在老式主板上），仍然需要寻找或囤积相关连接器，或者寻找物理不同但电气兼容的替代品。这里强调了连接器类型和兼容性的技术细节。

• [HeyLaughingBoy] 提到自己拥有一盒IDC Centronics打印机连接器，并表示会去查看它们在eBay上的市场价格。这反映了一些人对旧式连接器市场价值的关注，以及通过转售获取经济利益的可能性。

• [threeio] 分享了自己之前为NeXT电脑购买DB-19连接器的经历，并提到正品DB-19线缆价格昂贵。这里突出了DB-19线缆在特定设备上的高成本问题。

Bulk Lots of DB-19s for Sale!
June 30th, 2025 | Category:
Business
| Author: Steve
It’s time to relinquish my title as DB-19 king of the world and share some of my supply with other members of the vintage computing community, whether they’re repairing old machines, designing new devices, or even selling products that compete with BMOW. Yes, you heard that correctly. Nobody should need to resort to work-arounds like 3D-printing substitute DB-19’s when there already exists a supply of first quality, all-metal, professionally manufactured parts. So here we go!
Why do I have the world’s largest stockpile of DB-19 connectors? If you’ve never heard of the D-SUB DB-19, it’s a simple 19-pin connector that was common in Apple II, Macintosh, Atari, and NeXT computers from the 1980s. It later fell out of popularity, and manufacturers stopped making them in the 1990s. After the millenium when retrocomputing grew more popular, everybody snatched up the remaining supplies of DB-19s to use in their vintage computing projects, until there were none left.
In 2016 I gained some internet fame by commissioning an Asian factory to set up a new production line and
manufacture brand new DB-19 connectors
for the first time in the 21st century. Making it happen was a crazy adventure, but I had little alternative, because sales of the
BMOW Floppy Emu disk emulator
were taking off, and required a DB-19 in every device sold. Before long, I had unintentionally turned myself into the largest holder of DB-19 connectors anywhere, which I jealously guarded like a dragon sitting on its pile of gold. From time to time I got requests from other members of the vintage computer community asking to buy some of my hoard, but I usually said no. Sorry! I needed to ensure my own supply for BMOW.
Now it’s 2025, times are different, and I would prefer to see some of my stash reach other hands and other makers of vintage computer equipment. I’m selling the DB-19’s in large lots of 1000 pieces each, beginning with an eBay auction to help determine the level of interest and demand. The starting bid on the auction is equivalent to $0.44 each, which is an extreme bargain compared to the prices that they’ve sold for elsewhere in the last decade, if you could find them at all. I won’t be selling them individually or in small lots, but maybe somebody else will want to buy them in bulk and then flip them in small quantities for a nice profit. And if you have dreams for some massive number of DB-19 connectors, more than the lot that I’ve listed, talk to me.
The connectors offered for sale here were newly manufactured in 2024 for Big Mess o’ Wires, and are the same DB-19’s sold with the BMOW Floppy Emu and other BMOW products. They are DB-19 male, with solder cup terminals, sometimes called DB-19P. They are professionally manufactured by a D-SUB factory and have an all-metal shell. This is the connector itself (without shroud or other wires), and they can be used for making cables, or can also be edge-mounted on a 1.2mm or 1.6mm thick PCB as BMOW does. A footprint file for edge-mounting is available upon request. They are packaged in plastic trays of 50 pieces each, with 20 trays (1000 pieces) per box.
Interested?
The eBay auction listing is here
. Auction ends on Tuesday, July 8. Thanks for your interest!

data.title: Meta Joins Kotlin Foundation
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Meta宣布正式以金级会员身份加入Kotlin基金会，标志着其对Kotlin及Android开发生态的长期承诺。Meta工程师近年来将数千万行Java代码迁移至Kotlin，并开发了内部工具Kotlinator以自动化转换过程。此外，Meta通过开源项目如Buck2分享其工作，旨在提升构建速度和可扩展性。加入Kotlin基金会后，Meta将支持基金会的资助计划，促进开源库的发展和创新。此举体现了Meta对Kotlin社区及语言跨平台发展的支持。更多信息可访问Meta开源网站或关注其社交媒体。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kotlin及其多平台框架的流行度、复杂性以及与其他编程语言和技术的比较

不同观点：
• **支持Kotlin及多平台潜力的观点**：  
   - **grizzles**认为Kotlin及其Compose Multiplatform是非常优秀的技术，能够作为JavaScript的替代品，支持跨平台（如Web、iOS、Android、桌面、watchOS）的原生UI代码共享。  
   - 对于这种潜力没有被更广泛地认可和使用，grizzles表示惊讶。

• **对Kotlin复杂性的质疑**：  
   - **ksec**认为Kotlin和Swift都有过度复杂的问题，相比之下，Objective-C和Java已经足够好用。  
   - ksec对Kotlin的复杂性提出了质疑，认为这种复杂性可能是其未广泛流行的原因之一。

• **对Meta技术选择的关注**：  
   - **Apofis**简短表示对Meta使用Kotlin的认可，但没有深入讨论技术细节。  
   - **ksec**则进一步提出疑问，想知道Meta是否仍然在使用PHP或其衍生语言Hack，暗示对Meta技术选型的关注。

补充讨论：
• **技术流行度与实际应用**：  
   - grizzles对Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform未被广泛采用表示不解，暗示可能存在技术认知或推广上的问题。  
   - ksec则从技术复杂性和替代技术的角度进行分析，认为老技术如Objective-C和Java可能仍然有其市场。

• **争议焦点**：  
   - Kotlin的复杂性是否是其未广泛流行的原因。  
   - 不同开发者对技术复杂性与实用性的看法存在分歧。

总结来看，讨论主要围绕Kotlin及其多平台框架的潜力和实际应用情况，同时涉及其复杂性与技术选型的争议。

We are proud to announce that Meta has officially joined the
Kotlin Foundation
as a gold member, marking a significant milestone in our ongoing commitment to Kotlin and the broader Android development ecosystem.
Over the past several years, Meta engineers have been actively
migrating our extensive Android codebase
—comprising tens of millions of lines—from Java to Kotlin. To facilitate this massive transition, we developed an internal tool called
Kotlinator
, which automates much of the conversion process while ensuring the resulting Kotlin code is idiomatic and compatible with our internal frameworks. We have continued to share these efforts as a part of the
enterprise Java-to-Kotlin working group
.
In addition to these internal efforts, we at Meta have been sharing our work publicly through open source projects such as Kotlin and Android build toolchain in
Buck2
. Initiatives like this toolchain aim to provide
tooling and best practices
for enhancing build speeds and scalability, ultimately benefiting the broader developer community.
Meta’s involvement in the Kotlin Foundation aligns with our broader strategy to support and advance the Kotlin ecosystem. Meta will contribute to initiatives in the Kotlin Foundation’s grants program, which support open source library authors and encourage innovation among students and developers.
Meta’s membership in the Kotlin Foundation underscores our dedication to fostering a robust, collaborative Kotlin community and advancing the language’s capabilities across platforms.

Meta Open Source site
, subscribe to our
YouTube channel

.

data.title: Show HN: A continuation of IRS Direct File that can be self-hosted
data.author: elijahwright_
data.article_summary: OpenFile 是一个基于 IRS Direct File 的免费税务工具，提供了税务相关文件处理的功能。该项目使用 Docker 运行，通过执行 `docker compose up -d` 命令启动服务，客户端可在 `localhost:3000/df/file` 访问。项目主要使用 JavaScript、TypeScript、Java 等编程语言开发，代码托管在 GitHub 上，目前有 8 个星标和 1 个分支。详细信息和使用指南可访问官方文档：[https://docs.openfile.tax](https://docs.openfile.tax)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源税务相关文件工具的实用性、技术实现、支持情况以及相关政策问题。

不同观点：
• **对开源努力的赞赏与支持**：[nxobject] 感谢了项目团队的持续努力，并表达了对这种开源工具制度化的期望。同时指出了一个技术问题：在黑暗模式下文档页面显示有问题（黑底黑字）。

• **对政府表单流程的改进建议**：[onetom] 提出了一个更广泛的建议，希望个人能够存储自己的信息，并通过软件自动填写政府表单，甚至可以由公民自托管信息数据库，政府只需要查询即可。这一观点强调了政府流程的数字化和标准化。

• **对AI辅助税务的幽默建议**：[sciencesama] 以幽默的方式建议利用AI来帮助减少税收，虽然不是严肃的讨论，但也反映了公众对简化税务流程的期望。

• **对美国政府效率的批评**：[citizenpaul] 表达了对美国政府效率低下的不满，同时表示了对项目的支持，但也提到个人对避免使用JavaScript的偏好。

• **技术问题的反馈**：[onetom] 再次指出了一个具体的技术问题，即文档中的链接导致404错误。

• **对命令行工具的需求**：[EPWN3D] 表示希望有一个命令行工具，并提到如果有时间可能会自己开发，暗示了对项目功能扩展的兴趣。

• **对代码功能和适用范围的质疑**：[1oooqooq] 对开源代码的具体功能提出了疑问，质疑其是否仅适用于拥有单一W2表格且无股票收入的简单税务情况。

补充讨论：
• **政策信息的分享**：[hermannj314] 分享了一项法案内容，指出美国国税局的直接报税项目在法案通过后30天内被终止的可能性，暗示了该项目可能面临的政策风险。

争议焦点：
• **项目的适用范围和功能限制**：部分用户对开源项目的实际功能和适用范围存在疑问，尤其是对于复杂税务情况的处理能力。
• **政府效率和政策变化**：用户对美国政府在数字化和政策执行方面的效率表达了不满，并指出了政策变化可能对项目产生的影响。

总结：讨论主要围绕项目的技术实现、功能、政策支持以及用户对政府流程改进的期望展开，同时也涉及一些技术细节和政策信息的分享。

data.title: Abstraction boundaries are optimization boundaries
data.author: delifue
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了N+1查询问题及其由泄漏的抽象导致的原因，通常是由于ORM（对象关系映射）无法自动优化多次查询为单次查询。常见解决方案是降低抽象边界，明确指示ORM批量获取数据。然而，文章提出另一种思路：通过提升抽象边界，将ORM功能集成到语言中，使其能够通过重写规则（如合并N次查询为一次）进行优化。文章还以Haskell的流融合（stream fusion）为例，说明在声明式、纯函数式语言中，提升抽象边界有助于优化。文章总结了一个有趣的模式：提升抽象边界同时提升了优化边界。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于编译器优化、ORM（对象关系映射）工具以及抽象边界对优化的影响的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• **[discarded1023]**：认为Haskell等语言能够在模块和抽象边界之间进行优化，提到了Debray在链接时优化的工作以及JVM、MLton等全程序优化编译器的例子。同时指出，经典的数据抽象可以根据使用情况选择或优化实现，提到了2000年代初的相关研究。

• **[mrkeen]**：指出ORM存在“泄漏抽象”问题，导致无法自动优化查询，例如N+1问题。同时提到Haskell和SQL是声明式/纯函数式的，因此更易于优化，而ORM则不是。他还提到了Haxl作为解决方案。

• **[joshdata]**：质疑是否存在编译器解决方案来防止坏查询。建议通过明确标记函数类型或避免在循环中使用数据库连接来改善问题，强调了对数据库连接的显式管理。

• **[cogman10]**：认为编译器无法进行期望的优化，因为编译器不理解SQL和数据的存储方式，也无法感知数据集的当前状态。他指出，RDBMS通过大量统计数据进行优化，而编译器难以复制这种性能。

• **[wavemode]**：同意抽象边界是优化边界，但认为不需要将ORM查询变成语言的一部分来提高边界。以Django ORM为例，指出通过返回QuerySet等技术，可以让调用者有更多控制和优化机会。

• **[vjerancrnjak]**：主张避免使用ORM，认为其设计目标是封装而不是效率。建议使用更高效的方法预加载上下文，而不是依赖ORM的懒加载特性。

• **[nyrikki]**：认为ORM不是一个好的抽象例子，因为SQL的声明式模型与命令式编程存在阻抗不匹配。讨论了SQL隐藏复杂性以及不同持久化模型的权衡分析。

补充讨论：
• **Haxl作为N+1问题的解决方案**：[mrkeen]提到了Haxl作为解决N+1问题的实际案例，提供了一种优化的可能性。
• **全程序优化和编译器优化边界**：[discarded1023]提到了全程序优化编译器（如MLton）以及早期研究，表明编译器在某些情况下可以跨越抽象边界进行优化。
• **ORM设计的权衡**：[nyrikki]和[vjerancrnjak]都提到了ORM的设计初衷是封装和易用性，而非效率，因此在效率问题上可能需要考虑其他方案。

争议焦点：
• ORM的效率和设计权衡：一部分评论者（如[vjerancrnjak]和[nyrikki]）认为ORM的设计初衷和效率之间存在矛盾，主张避免使用ORM。
• 编译器优化的可行性：[cogman10]和[joshdata]对编译器能否解决坏查询问题持怀疑态度，而[discarded1023]和[wavemode]则认为在某些情况下编译器或语言特性可以帮助优化。

总结：讨论围绕ORM的效率问题、编译器优化的可行性以及不同编程语言和工具在处理数据库查询优化时的表现展开。争议的核心在于ORM的设计是否适合高效查询，以及编译器能否有效解决查询优化问题。

44404831.article_content:
Abstraction boundaries are optimization boundaries
The N+1 query problem occurs when your application code sends one SQL query per element in a collection. The N queries are redundant; since all of the data is in the database already, a single query should be enough.
This problem is usually caused by a leaky abstraction; the ORM, or whatever database abstraction you are using, can’t anticipate that it would need to send N queries, so it can’t automatically optimize this down to a single query. The solution is usually to move the abstraction boundary
down
, and explicitly tell the ORM that you will need to fetch a set of rows in bulk, rather than repeatedly fetching single rows.
But what if we could do it the other way around? Can we solve the problem by moving the abstraction boundary
up
instead?
The problem with the ORM example is that the compiler doesn’t know what the ORM does, and as such it can’t optimize it; to the compiler it’s just another piece of userland code. However, what if we raise the abstraction boundary and make the ORM part of the language? This means that we could formulate rewrite rules for the ORM, allowing it to eg merge the N queries into a single query.
There are other examples of this: Haskell has support for adding rewrite rule pragmas to libraries; among other things this is used to optimize list operations using
stream fusion
. However, this only works since Haskell is declarative / pure; the low-level operational semantics (like evaluation order) are abstracted away from the programmer, and as such are amenable to optimization.
I think there’s an interesting pattern here: By raising the abstraction boundary we have also raised the optimization boundary.

主要讨论点：Stripe账户迁移服务的可行性、定价、技术与法律问题以及隐私和数据保护

不同观点：
• egorfine建议提高价格，因为该服务是一次性交易，且对有需求的客户至关重要，他还提出按客户数量定价的建议。
• x13关注商标和标志的使用问题，担心在服务中使用Stripe的标志可能会引发法律问题。
• janmo分享了自己两年前类似的经历，指出Stripe在迁移和B2B功能上的不足，如缺乏公司名称字段和发票更正功能。
• e28eta作为Stripe的前员工，指出潜在的问题包括账户接管和Stripe API版本变更的长期管理。
• mtmail提到他们五年前的经历，Stripe的客户服务帮助复制了客户数据，但订阅需要手动处理。
• matthewtse分享了自己进行跨国账户迁移的艰难经历，并建议将服务目标定位为B2B工具，同时建立声誉。
• citizenpaul认为这种迁移服务可能是一个小众市场，服务商需要高收费才能盈利，并建议改变定价模型。
• absoluteunit1对跨国切换的复杂性表示关注，并表示未来可能会用到相关服务。
• kundi担心隐私和数据保护问题，强调处理Stripe账户时需要高度的谨慎和数据保护。
• xyst认为Stripe应该原生支持这种迁移功能，并希望被收购以实现此功能。
• Horffupolde质疑Stripe是否允许这种迁移服务。
• elemeno指出网站上的语法错误，建议将"transfers everything seamless"改为"seamlessly"。
• pxue质疑为什么选择这种方法而不是使用记录商户。
• joshstrange建议更改服务名称，因为包含“Stripe”可能会引发麻烦。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是服务名称中包含“Stripe”是否会引发法律问题，部分评论者如x13和joshstrange对此表示担忧。
• 另一个讨论点是服务的定价策略，egorfine和citizenpaul提出了不同的定价建议，包括按客户数量定价和针对B2B市场的定价策略。
• 技术问题如API版本变更和数据迁移的具体操作也被多次提及，e28eta和mtmail分享了他们的经验和见解。
• 隐私和数据保护也是一个重要的讨论点，kundi强调了处理Stripe账户时需要高度的谨慎和数据保护措施。

data.title: Show HN: Jobs by Referral: Find jobs in your LinkedIn network
data.author: nicksergeant
data.article_summary:
JobsByReferral.com帮助用户通过LinkedIn网络寻找工作机会。它通过分析用户下载的LinkedIn数据，找到用户 connections 所在公司的职位空缺，从而增加被推荐和获得面试的机会。具体步骤包括：

1. 下载LinkedIn数据档案（通过“数据隐私”设置获取完整数据，包括Connections.csv文件）。
2. 可选择使用demo数据体验功能。
3. 上传LinkedIn数据文件（ZIP格式或Connections.csv文件）开始搜索。

该工具旨在利用已有的人脉网络，提高求职成功率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LinkedIn网络内搜索功能及其相关问题

不同观点：
• Gergely和Floutist44认为LinkedIn已经存在"在你的网络中"的搜索过滤功能，且该功能已使用多年，新的AI搜索只是让这个功能更加智能化。
• Hackernewds对该功能表示赞赏，认为这是LinkedIn早就应该开发的功能。

• Thih9关注个人数据隐私问题，询问数据是否被存储或用于其他目的，是否有隐私政策保护用户数据。
• B8提到在其他平台如Blind上可以获得推荐，但质疑LinkedIn上随机添加的人是否会真正提供推荐。
• Fuzzy1000建议增加一个功能，可以精确定位和分析人际网络中的连接。
• Orliesaurus将这个功能比作Blind的升级版。
• Dijit提出相反的需求，希望有一个推荐之前共事过的优秀同事给当前公司的功能，并描述了自己曾经尝试开发该功能的经历。
• Shados认为这个功能展示了AI将如何彻底改变行业，并讨论了LinkedIn内部可能的产品开发流程，强调外部开发者能更快实现新功能。
• Bsoles关注数据安全问题，引用LinkedIn要求用户下载和提供整个LinkedIn数据的做法，提出担忧。
• Toyg对功能实现方式提出质疑，认为这是在让用户进行LinkedIn数据抓取，建议使用官方API，并指出该服务在GDPR合规性上的重大影响。

补充讨论：
• 数据隐私和合规性是讨论中的一个重要问题，特别是对于欧洲用户的GDPR合规性。
• 功能的实现方式引起了一些争议，特别是关于使用官方API和用户数据抓取的问题。
• 对功能的实际效果和用户使用习惯存在不同看法，例如对不活跃用户档案的过滤效果和推荐的真实性。

• Dijit提出相反的需求，希望有一个推荐之前共事过的优秀同事给当前公司的功能，并描述了自己曾经尝试开发该功能的经历。
• Shados认为这个功能展示了AI将如何彻底改变行业，并讨论了LinkedIn内部可能的产品开发流程，强调外部开发者能更快实现新功能。
• Bsoles关注数据安全问题，引用LinkedIn要求用户下载和提供整个LinkedIn数据的做法，提出担忧。
• Toyg对功能实现方式提出质疑，认为这是在让用户进行LinkedIn数据抓取，建议使用官方API，并指出该服务在GDPR合规性上的重大影响。

补充讨论：
• 数据隐私和合规性是讨论中的一个重要问题，特别是对于欧洲用户的GDPR合规性。
• 功能的实现方式引起了一些争议，特别是关于使用官方API和用户数据抓取的问题。
• 对功能的实际效果和用户使用习惯存在不同看法，例如对不活跃用户档案的过滤效果和推荐的真实性。

data.title: Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna – Nuclear propulsion and solar sailing
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了利用先进推进技术前往太阳系边缘天体塞德娜的可行性。研究评估了两种推进方案：基于D-³He热核聚变的直接融合驱动（DFD）火箭引擎，以及利用涂层热脱附进行推进的太阳帆。对于DFD方案，分析假设了一个1.6兆瓦的系统，能够实现约10年抵达塞德娜，其中包括1.5年的持续推力。而对于太阳帆，则考虑通过木星引力辅助进行飞越，预计7年完成任务。研究还考虑了有效载荷能力、旅行时间、科学回报以及通信限制等关键参数。结果为未来深空探测任务规划提供了基础对比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sedna探测任务的可行性及相关推进技术（尤其是直接融合驱动技术）的发展现状和前景

不同观点：
• **pavel_lishin** 对Direct Fusion Drive（DFD）的实际进展表示怀疑，特别是其可靠性和能否在太空长时间运行。同时指出，鉴于Sedna的轨道特性，传统推进系统需要长达30年的深空旅行，因此任务需要尽快启动。
• **myrmidon** 认为DFD是一个有趣的概念，可能为未来的星际旅行提供可能性，但对DFD如何选择D/He3融合而不是D/D融合表示困惑，并担心中子辐射问题。
• **mikewarot** 提到了过去的核裂变项目（如Project Rover），认为近期的核系统可能更可行，并指出在轨的OTP-2卫星已经使用了创新的推进系统，包括“融合增强”的离子推进器。
• **stevenAthompson** 提出了一种替代方案，建议发射大量小型网状探测器，利用数量优势和低成本（类似手机成本）来弥补单个探测器的性能不足。
• **pier25** 认为即使使用DFD，到达Sedna也需要长达40年的时间线，质疑是否有组织能够长期维持这样的项目预算和规划。
• **jmyeet** 对所有提到的推进技术持怀疑态度，认为目前的技术都处于非常初期的阶段，尚未经过实际验证，特别是核推进技术。此外，对长时间任务中探测器的生存能力和太阳帆的耐久性表示担忧，并建议将资源投入到天王星或海王星的探测任务中。

补充讨论：
• **accrual** 认为Sedna的远距离探测可能揭示其表面分子的意外信息，有助于理解其起源和远处的太空环境。
• **ananddtyagi** 以《三体》小说作类比，暗示任务的复杂性和科幻性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于当前推进技术（尤其是DFD）的实际可行性和成熟度，以及长时间深空任务中探测器的生存能力与任务规划的现实性。

Title:
Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna -- Nuclear propulsion and advanced solar sailing concepts
Authors:
Elena Ancona
,
Roman Ya. Kezerashvili
,
Savino Longo
View a PDF of the paper titled Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna -- Nuclear propulsion and advanced solar sailing concepts, by Elena Ancona and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Exploring the outer reaches of the Solar System presents significant propulsion and mission design challenges. This study assesses the feasibility of a mission to Sedna using two advanced propulsion concepts: the Direct Fusion Drive (DFD) rocket engine, based on D-$^{3}$He thermonuclear fusion, and a solar sail utilizing thermal desorption of its coating for propulsion. Both are evaluated for a one-way Earth-to-Sedna mission; however, due to the different performances the DFD would enable orbit insertion, whereas for the solar sail a flyby is envisioned. The analysis evaluates key mission parameters, including delivered payload capacity, travel time, and potential science return. For the DFD, we assume a 1.6 MW system with constant thrust and specific impulse, while for the solar sail, we consider acceleration via thermal desorption and a gravity-assist maneuver around Jupiter. The mission analysis incorporates four key phases: departure, interplanetary acceleration, interplanetary coasting, and rendezvous. Sedna is expected to pass through the perihelion of its orbit in 2075--2076 and then move again away from the Sun. Considering the distances involved, a mission targeting the object would need to be launched "relatively" soon, especially if using conventional propulsion systems, which could require up to 30 years of deep-space travel. In our study, results indicate that the DFD could reach Sedna in approximately 10 years, with 1.5 years of thrusting, while the solar sail, assisted by Jupiter's gravity, could complete the journey in 7 years. The feasibility of science payload accommodation, power availability, and communication constraints is also considered. These findings provide a comparative foundation for future deep-space mission planning.

data.title: Aesop in Words of One Syllable
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 《Aesop in Words of One Syllable》是一本独特的儿童读物，出版于19世纪，属于玛丽·戈多芬（Mary Godolphin）创作的“单音节”系列。该书用简单的单音节词汇重写了伊索寓言，旨在让孩子们更容易阅读。玛丽·戈多芬本名露西·艾金（Lucy Aikin），是英国著名的历史学家、诗人和女性主义者，对儿童教育有浓厚兴趣。这本书包含99个寓言故事，如《狼来了》和《狐狸与葡萄》，但像《龟兔赛跑》等故事因无法用单音节词表达而未收录。该书通过Distributed Proofreaders和Project Gutenberg等志愿者项目得以保存和传播。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用单音节词语的词典及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [alnwlsn] 介绍了一个包含约2500个单音节词的词典，并提供了几个例子。该用户认为这种词典很有趣且独特，但并未深入讨论其有效性或应用场景。
   
• [pinko] 认为该词典的作者在某些地方作弊，例如使用连字符将多音节词（如"butch-ers"）分割成单音节，质疑其纯粹性。

• [teraflop] 猜测该词典可能启发了Guy Steele的"Growing a Language"演讲，或两者独立得出了相似的概念，提供了相关视频链接。

• [gweinberg] 质疑坚持使用单音节词的必要性，认为使用常见词即可，并指出人们最早学习的词汇通常是双音节的，如重复的音节。

• [esafak] 支持使用简化语言的想法，并分享了自己与孩子阅读维多利亚时代翻译版本的困难，认为现代儿童可能难以理解复杂的语言结构，提供了具体例子。

• [cckolon] 提到Randall Monroe对简单英语的痴迷，通过链接引用xkcd漫画，暗示单音节词语的应用在其他领域也有体现。

• [josefritzishere] 提供了背景信息，指出该类书籍有一个系列，并提到某些书籍通过连字符化来满足单音节标准，提供了相关历史出版信息和链接。

• [JKCalhoun] 更喜欢在Archive.org而非Project Gutenberg上查看该类书籍，并个人对每篇故事末尾的道德总结表示不喜欢。

• [vintermann] 分享了自己用单音节词做游戏的经历，但认为这种方法作为儿童教育工具不太实用，因为一旦不小心使用了多音节词，就可能导致困惑，且认为这不是必须遵循的规则。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于单音节词词典的纯粹性和实用性。部分用户质疑作者是否严格遵循了单音节规则，以及这种方法在实际教育中的有效性。

• 不同用户对简化语言的看法各异，有的认为有助于儿童理解，有的则认为现代儿童难以理解复杂的古代语言结构。

• 用户们还分享了相关资源和背景信息，丰富了讨论的深度和广度。

44433843.article_content:
Hot off the Press
Book Reviews and News from Distributed Proofreaders
Home
About
Aesop in Words of One Syllable
In the 19th Century, British and American children’s literature evolved from puritanical moral and religious instruction to delightfully imaginative tales meant to awaken a sense of wonder. But morality and imagination could certainly thrive together.
Æsop’s Fables in Words of One Syllable
is an excellent example of this.
The ancient Greek storyteller
Aesop
may or may not have existed, and he may or may not have written the hundreds of morality tales attributed to him. Yet his stories have been popular from the time of Aristotle to the present day, and their morals have contributed classic expressions like “sour grapes” to the English language. The first English version, printed by William Caxton in 1484, was intended for adults. In the 16th and 17th Centuries, English schoolboys were taught Latin and English from various translations of the fables. It wasn’t until the 18th Century that the fables began to appear in illustrated editions intended to entertain (while edifying) children. And in the 19th Century, with the flowering of children’s literature, there was a veritable explosion of illustrated Aesops.
Æsop’s Fables in Words of One Syllable
is unique among the illustrated editions: It’s written entirely in words of one syllable (except for the title, of course). It’s part of a “One Syllable” series written between 1867 and 1870 by Mary Godolphin, the pen name of
Lucy Aikin
. Aikin was a prominent English historian, poet, and feminist who also took a keen interest in the education of children. Other books in her “One Syllable” series include
Robinson Crusoe
,
The Swiss Family Robinson
, and
The Pilgrim’s Progress
. They’re all designed to make reading them easy for children.
The Aesop volume, in an 1895 edition published after Aikin’s death, contains 99 fables, including those featuring the boy who cried wolf, the fox and the grapes, and the goose that laid the golden (“gold”) egg. Notably absent are “The Tortoise and the Hare” and “The Ant and the Grasshopper,” perhaps because Aikin couldn’t come up with one-syllable synonyms for some of those creatures. But there’s plenty here to enjoy, thanks to the volunteers at Distributed Proofreaders and Project Gutenberg.
This post was contributed by Linda Cantoni, a Distributed Proofreaders volunteer.

data.title: Converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules
data.author: vblanco
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了将大型数学软件包从C++转换为使用C++20模块系统的经验。传统上，C++软件包通过头文件定义接口，这种方式效率低下。C++20引入了模块系统，通过导出和导入机制提高编译效率。作者以一个包含约80万行代码的有限元库为例，描述了一种同时支持头文件和模块接口的转换方法，讨论了遇到的挑战和实际效果。结果显示，虽然转换需要一定努力，但能有效减少库本身的编译时间，而下游项目的编译时间变化不明显。文章最后探讨了未来几十年内整个数学软件生态系统转换到模块系统的长期策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：模块化对编译时间和代码结构的影响，以及与其他优化方法（如预编译头文件、LLMs应用）的比较

不同观点：
• npalli认为，模块化在减少编译时间（约10%）和改善代码结构方面有明显的好处，但对下游项目的编译时间影响不明确。他还提到，对于现有代码（如deal.II）的模块化可能不如从零开始设计模块化有效，并指出通过其他方法（如pch、forward decls）可能获得更大性能提升。

• trostaft对作者（Wolfgang）及其团队在计算数学和研究软件方面的成就表示赞赏，并期待阅读其作品，显示出对作者专业性的信任和期待。

• nsoonhui提出，LLMs可能有助于将遗留的Fortran或COBOL程序转换为现代语言，认为这种任务应该是LLMs的强项，因为语法和需求明确，且输出可验证。

• barchar指出，模块化主要帮助解析时间，而非代码生成时间，并可能因内联和全局优化的增加而负面影响代码生成性能。他还提到，当依赖项未模块化时，会出现大的全局模块片段，增加BMI大小和解析时间，并指出当前构建系统对头文件单元支持不足的问题。

• Asooka希望看到模块化与预编译头文件的比较，怀疑预编译头文件可能以更少的工作量提供相同的编译时间收益。

• isatty仅对代码块的样式表示不满，未深入讨论技术内容。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及模块化对不同编译阶段的影响，以及当前工具链（如构建系统、编译器）对模块化支持的不足。
• 对于遗留代码的模块化改造和LLMs在代码转换中的潜在应用也有一定的讨论。
• 预编译头文件作为模块化的替代方案被提及，显示出对不同优化方法的权衡和选择的关注。

Computer Science > Software Engineering

[Submitted on 26 Jun 2025]
Title:
Experience converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules
Authors:
Wolfgang Bangerth
View a PDF of the paper titled Experience converting a large mathematical software package written in C++ to C++20 modules, by Wolfgang Bangerth
View PDF
Abstract:
Mathematical software has traditionally been built in the form of "packages" that build on each other. A substantial fraction of these packages is written in C++ and, as a consequence, the interface of a package is described in the form of header files that downstream packages and applications can then #include. C++ has inherited this approach towards exporting interfaces from C, but the approach is clunky, unreliable, and slow. As a consequence, C++20 has introduced a "module" system in which packages explicitly export declarations and code that compilers then store in machine-readable form and that downstream users can "import" -- a system in line with what many other programming languages have used for decades.
Herein, I explore how one can convert large mathematical software packages written in C++ to this system, using the
this http URL
finite element library with its around 800,000 lines of code as an example. I describe an approach that allows providing both header-based and module-based interfaces from the same code base, discuss the challenges one encounters, and how modules actually work in practice in a variety of technical and human metrics. The results show that with a non-trivial, but also not prohibitive effort, the conversion to modules is possible, resulting in a reduction in compile time for the converted library itself; on the other hand, for downstream projects, compile times show no clear trend. I end with thoughts about long-term strategies for converting the entire ecosystem of mathematical software over the coming years or decades.

data.title: What should a native DOM templating API look like?
data.author: jdkoeck
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了创建一个声明式JavaScript DOM模板API的设想。该API旨在让开发者描述他们想要的DOM结构，而不是如何实现。它类似于JSX和lit-html等语法，专注于模板的创建和更新，而不涉及组件。这个API必须符合多项约束，如保持网页兼容性、不引入破坏性变化、不影响现有网站性能，以及保持低安全风险。此外，该API应直接可用且易于使用，无需编译器，并与现有JavaScript和DOM平台保持一致。其核心目标是为框架提供一个原始模板功能，使其能够在其上构建组件。关键要求包括API的人体工程学设计和可供JavaScript库内部使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript客户端应用的模板和渲染方案选择，涉及不同的框架和技术，如lit-html、Svelte、React、Signals、VDOM等。

不同观点：
• **支持使用lit-html**：[polyrand]认为lit-html的`html`和`render`函数简单、方便、快速，特别是因为它缓存了渲染部分，状态改变时重新渲染性能也不错。同时，使用Vanilla JS使得组件只是使用`html`模板字符串的函数，易于组合和理解，比React更容易推理。

• **支持Svelte**：[maxloh]提出Svelte的语法更具可读性，并给出示例代码展示Svelte的简洁性。对没有提及Svelte表示不解。

• **支持Tagged Template Literals**：[vlucas]强烈支持使用Tagged Template Literals进行模板渲染，认为这是最简单且原生的JavaScript方案，尤其在与native Signals结合时效果很好。他还提到服务端渲染也主要依赖字符串，因此模板使用字符串是合理且高效的。

• **对模板字符串和AST的讨论**：[bevr1337]认为嵌套函数调用或基于对象的API不够“像HTML”，并讨论了模板字符串和AST处理的挑战，提到函数接收未解析的HTML字符串和已计算的表达式，需要进一步处理。

• **批评设计基于VDOM机制**：[MrJohz]批评该设计没有探索Svelte、Vue Vapor或SolidJS的工作原理，认为其依赖于渲染是廉价操作的假设，并指出信号机制框架（如SolidJS）能更有效地避免不必要的渲染。他还质疑该设计的目标用户和实际应用场景。

• **对属性和事件命名空间的建议**：[svieira]不满意使用不同符号来区分属性、事件等，认为JavaScript不像Perl或K语言，应该采用更符合JavaScript习惯的命名空间方式，如`on:`、`attr:`等。

• **简化框架，避免编译器和属性黑客**：[rglover]认为许多流行框架过于依赖属性黑客和编译器，而直接使用HTML字符串加上一些抽象就能构建出健壮的UI框架，并分享了自己的项目[1]。

补充讨论：
• **对安全性的担忧**：[dvh]强调默认应是安全的，避免像`innerHTML = user_name`这样的字符串拼接，以防止安全漏洞。

• **对模板语言的批评**：[timewizard]最喜欢Amrita模板库，认为将代码和元素混合在一起的模板语言脆弱且难以扩展，提倡将DOM和逻辑分开处理。

• **其他评论**：[hk1337]称赞文章字体大，考虑在自己的博客中效仿。[RadiozRadioz]认为这种方案会像XSLT。

争议焦点：
• **模板字符串 vs. AST/VDOM**：关于模板字符串处理的便捷性与AST处理复杂性之间的争议。
• **不同框架的优劣**：如Svelte的可读性与React/Lit的VDOM机制对比，信号机制框架（如SolidJS）与传统VDOM机制的效率讨论。
• **命名和语法的习惯**：对属性和事件命名空间的符号选择存在不同意见。

44436290.article_content:
If you read my previous post,
The time is right for a DOM templating API
, you might be wondering what such an API would look like.
Let's dive into that question now.
What are we building?
First, let's clarify what we're trying to design here, because when people hear the abstract template API idea described, before there's a concrete proposal or examples, they can sometimes think of very different things.
In
webcomponents/1069
I propose that we add a "declarative JavaScript templating API"
Declarative means that the developer is describing
what
they want, not
how
to achieve it. What exactly constitutes "declarative" is often debatable, and under every declarative API is an imperative implementation, but hopefully people can align on the spirit of the word.
By "templating" we mean the ability to describe the DOM that the developer wants to create and update in a form that resembles the output. This includes syntaxes like JSX and lit-html, which for some people count as something other than templating. For our purposes, they are.
Taken together, "declarative DOM templating" is something that is very, very common. All major frameworks today have declarative templating at their core.
But we're going to narrow our focus a bit
JavaScript
APIs.
By "JavaScript API" we mean methods, classes, etc. that are part of the overall DOM JavaScript API surface. Something that's a sibling and alternative to
innerHTML
,
importNode()
, and a bunch of other DOM APIs that web developers and frameworks use to create and update DOM. But also, we mean that script-like abilities will be left to JavaScript, not added to markup.
It's also important to not that we're not talking about components at all, just templated DOM creation and updating. Most frameworks intertwine the two concepts, so some people aren't aware that there can be a distinction. One of the use cases for this proposal is to be a primitive that frameworks can use, so it's necessary that components can be added on top of templates, but any such feature to do that should be as generic and minimal as possible.
What's guiding us?
In my experience, we can derive the general API shape for this feature from its constraints and requirements, with a dash of opinion about good APIs on top. Listing these helps us see what things must be a certain way vs which things can flex as part of the decision space for the problem.
Constraints
Because we're designing a native DOM API, and not a framework, we have more constraints to deal with. A native API has to work within the current platform, can't break existing sites, and has to be viable within the standards process.
Web compatibility: The proposal can't introduce any breaking changes to the platform.
Standard file types: While a proposal could introduce a new file type just for templates, that's unlikely to make it through the web standards process without incredibly compelling reasons. We'll take using the existing file types as a hard constraint.
Standard JavaScript: It's also possible to try to simultaneously introduce changes to both the DOM and JavaScript, but this is also less likely to succeed because we would be dealing with two separate standards bodies and a much larger overall addition to the platform.
JavaScript is not just a web language anymore, and the JavaScript side would likely have to be useful for non-web use-cases to move forward, dramatically raising the complexity of a proposal.
So we'll also take it as a hard constraint that this API works with today's standard JavaScript.
Low implementation security risk: The proposal should not require drastic and potentially-unsafe HTML parser changes. Implementors are just extremely reluctant to make large HTML parser changes, since they are prime targets for attackers and previous changes (like
<template>
)
did
introduce security bugs.
No performance regressions on existing sites. Slowing down existing sites, or benchmarks like Speedometer, will sink a proposal when it's implemented.
Security: New APIs have a much higher security bar to clear than previous platform changes. They need to be secure by default.
No required compiler: This is not universal, but many web platform maintainers insist that web APIs should be directly usable by developers and not require a compiler to be useful. This does not preclude an API from being a good compile target for alternate syntaxes.
Coherence with the platform. Also not universal, but it will be drastically easier to get a proposal accepted if it's coherent with the existing platform. This would prevent us from introducing a new "better DOM", for instance.

Ergonomic API: This API should be nice to use directly for developers.

44436290.article_summary: 本文讨论了创建一个声明式JavaScript DOM模板API的设想。该API旨在让开发者描述他们想要的DOM结构，而不是如何实现。它类似于JSX和lit-html等语法，专注于模板的创建和更新，而不涉及组件。这个API必须符合多项约束，如保持网页兼容性、不引入破坏性变化、不影响现有网站性能，以及保持低安全风险。此外，该API应直接可用且易于使用，无需编译器，并与现有JavaScript和DOM平台保持一致。其核心目标是为框架提供一个原始模板功能，使其能够在其上构建组件。关键要求包括API的人体工程学设计和可供JavaScript库内部使用。
44436290.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript客户端应用的模板和渲染方案选择，涉及不同的框架和技术，如lit-html、Svelte、React、Signals、VDOM等。

不同观点：
• **支持使用lit-html**：[polyrand]认为lit-html的`html`和`render`函数简单、方便、快速，特别是因为它缓存了渲染部分，状态改变时重新渲染性能也不错。同时，使用Vanilla JS使得组件只是使用`html`模板字符串的函数，易于组合和理解，比React更容易推理。

• **支持Svelte**：[maxloh]提出Svelte的语法更具可读性，并给出示例代码展示Svelte的简洁性。对没有提及Svelte表示不解。

• **支持Tagged Template Literals**：[vlucas]强烈支持使用Tagged Template Literals进行模板渲染，认为这是最简单且原生的JavaScript方案，尤其在与native Signals结合时效果很好。他还提到服务端渲染也主要依赖字符串，因此模板使用字符串是合理且高效的。

• **对模板字符串和AST的讨论**：[bevr1337]认为嵌套函数调用或基于对象的API不够“像HTML”，并讨论了模板字符串和AST处理的挑战，提到函数接收未解析的HTML字符串和已计算的表达式，需要进一步处理。

• **批评设计基于VDOM机制**：[MrJohz]批评该设计没有探索Svelte、Vue Vapor或SolidJS的工作原理，认为其依赖于渲染是廉价操作的假设，并指出信号机制框架（如SolidJS）能更有效地避免不必要的渲染。他还质疑该设计的目标用户和实际应用场景。

• **对属性和事件命名空间的建议**：[svieira]不满意使用不同符号来区分属性、事件等，认为JavaScript不像Perl或K语言，应该采用更符合JavaScript习惯的命名空间方式，如`on:`、`attr:`等。

• **简化框架，避免编译器和属性黑客**：[rglover]认为许多流行框架过于依赖属性黑客和编译器，而直接使用HTML字符串加上一些抽象就能构建出健壮的UI框架，并分享了自己的项目[1]。

补充讨论：
• **对安全性的担忧**：[dvh]强调默认应是安全的，避免像`innerHTML = user_name`这样的字符串拼接，以防止安全漏洞。

• **对模板语言的批评**：[timewizard]最喜欢Amrita模板库，认为将代码和元素混合在一起的模板语言脆弱且难以扩展，提倡将DOM和逻辑分开处理。

• **其他评论**：[hk1337]称赞文章字体大，考虑在自己的博客中效仿。[RadiozRadioz]认为这种方案会像XSLT。

争议焦点：
• **模板字符串 vs. AST/VDOM**：关于模板字符串处理的便捷性与AST处理复杂性之间的争议。
• **不同框架的优劣**：如Svelte的可读性与React/Lit的VDOM机制对比，信号机制框架（如SolidJS）与传统VDOM机制的效率讨论。
• **命名和语法的习惯**：对属性和事件命名空间的符号选择存在不同意见。

data.title: Show HN: HackerNewt – Breadth-first exploring HN client for iOS
data.author: hnand
data.article_summary: HackerNewt是一款第三方Hacker News客户端，通过独特的评论树展示方式，解决传统界面评论过窄和层级不清的问题。其优点包括：评论宽度保持不变、始终显示当前评论的父评论、通过滑动控制子树浏览，以及轻松跳过不感兴趣的子树。此外，应用还提供自定义板块、搜索、阅读列表等功能，提升阅读体验。不过，部分用户反馈应用曾出现加载问题，但开发者迅速修复。该应用不隶属于Hacker News官网，隐私保护良好，免费下载但包含内购。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Hacker News的第三方应用及其功能改进建议

不同观点：
• goodburb建议添加一个持久保存的过滤功能，用于过滤特定话题（如政治或AI），并提到目前使用的替代工具。
• pvg引用了2年前的一个相关讨论，暗示该问题或类似功能建议早已存在。

• krishnasangeeth提到自己曾开发过类似应用，并分享了其应用链接，指出其应用风格与官网相似，且包含一些独特的交互设计。

• thebruce87m将该应用与HACK进行比较，表达了对HACK长期存在崩溃问题的失望，暗示可能考虑切换应用。
• vrighter对应用的创新性提出质疑，认为其设计类似于默认折叠的树状视图，要求进一步解释差异。
• xp84表示已经使用了该应用的早期版本，并对替代方案的出现表示欢迎，感谢社区开发者的贡献。

• recov提到应用在刷新 feeds 时较慢的问题，怀疑是HN本身的问题而非应用问题。
• sneak对应用不监控用户数据表示感谢，并提到已购买高级版本以支持开发者。
• fraXis询问是否会发布Android版本，显示了对跨平台支持的关注。
• mittermayr对应用的付费模式提出批评，认为通过限制基础功能（如暗黑模式）来收费不太合理，建议通过独特功能来吸引用户付费。
• ashish01提到自己实现了BFS扩展评论的功能，并分享了一个支持暗黑模式的网页应用链接。
• vednig提到自己也在React Native上开发了一个类似应用，暗示该领域开发者较多且方案多样。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：应用的创新性及付费模式。vrighter质疑应用的创新性，而mittermayr则批评了付费模式的不合理性。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：用户对HN现有问题的反馈（如afro88提到的bug及recov提到的刷新速度问题），以及跨平台支持和暗黑模式的需求（fraXis和ashish01的评论）。

Don't get lost in big Hacker News discussions!
HackerNewt is a Hacker News client that uses an alternative way of displaying comment tree. Advantages over traditional interfaces:
- Comment width doesn't get narrower no matter how deep in the tree you are

data.title: Graph Theory Applications in Video Games
data.author: haywirez
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了Clara Nguyễn关于图论在电子游戏中应用的演讲内容。演讲涵盖了图论的基本概念及其在游戏开发中的实际应用，包括：3D图形的顶点和边如何在图形中表示和处理，赛车游戏中的圈数计算，利用并查集生成迷宫，以及bitDP理论的应用等。演讲还讨论了1982年Atari 2600游戏《Entombed》中的一个未解问题。演讲时长为60-75分钟，内容深入，并包含与听众的互动。文章还提供了几个技术性问题及其答案，以帮助听众理解演讲内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Graph Theory在视频游戏中的应用及其具体实现方法

不同观点：
• [j2kun] 认为Graph Theory在视频游戏中的应用不仅仅限于理论，有许多实际应用，例如在视频游戏中的路径寻找等。然而，他指出文章中提到的某些应用似乎更偏向于假设性，缺乏实际使用证据。虽然作者没有提供这些技术在游戏设计中被实际应用的证明，但[j2kun]仍然肯定了作者提出这些想法的贡献，只是认为标题和引言具有误导性。

• [Llamamoe] 指出文章遗漏了图形语法（graph grammar）在关卡生成中的应用，特别是由游戏Unexplored首创的关卡生成算法。他认为这是一种非常吸引人的程序化生成（procgen）算法，值得讨论。

• [palmfacehn] 强调了在大型房间和走廊网络中寻找路径的明显应用，认为这是Graph Theory在游戏中的一个直接而实用的例子。

• [tantalor] 对文章未提及平面性（planarity）表示失望，暗示平面性作为Graph Theory的一个概念，在视频游戏中可能具有潜在的应用价值。

补充讨论：
• 文章标题和内容的匹配度是[j2kun]提出的一个争议点，他认为标题和引言可能误导读者以为所有提到的应用都是已被实际使用的技术。
• [Llamamoe]补充了图形语法关卡生成的具体实例，增加了对实际应用案例的讨论。
• [palmfacehn]通过具体场景（大型房间和走廊网络中的路径寻找）进一步论证了Graph Theory的实际应用。
• [tantalor]提出了对平面性的关注，虽然没有详细展开，但提示了这一概念在游戏设计中的潜在应用。

总体来看，讨论围绕Graph Theory在视频游戏中的实际应用和假设应用展开，参与者提供了不同的具体应用实例和概念，并对文章内容的全面性提出了看法。

SETTINGS

Talk #5										-
Graph Theory Applications in Video Games
Description:
A detailed look at Graph Theory and how it can be applied to video games.
Slogan:
There's more to this than you think...
Presenters:
Clara Nguyễn
Type:
Class Presentation
Date Originally Presented:
2020/03/11
Downloads:
[
Slides (Formal)
]

Slides (Original)
]
Talk Summary & Table of Contents
Graph Theory isn't just a topic that is restricted to being
"theory". There are several real-life applications of it. One of
those just happens to be video games. In this talk, I go over a
brief overview of several concepts where Graph Theory is applied.
The topics covered vary a bit:
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
-
Vertices in 3D space, how they are represented, and the
"rules" of dealing with vertices and edges.
Race Games & Lap Counting
-
Racing games where circuits are used to count laps, as
well as a mention of
Mario Kart Wii
and its Ultra-Shortcuts, to encourage
the simplicity of Hamiltonian Circuit checking for lap
counting.
Maze Generation w/ Disjoint-Sets & Union-Find
-
I talk about how to generate mazes efficiently, as well as
taking it a step up. Generation of multiple connected mazes
along with multi-floor/dimensional mazes are described. The
true power of the Disjoint-Set data structure with
optimisations is also discussed in depth.
bitDP, a theoretical approach
-
As a bonus, a theoretical "Part 2" to
my bitDP talk
is
included too. I talk about the theory behind it and how it
can be applied to a game to optimally guarantee that a
Hamiltonian Path exists in a generated graph.
Entombed (1982 Atari 2600 game)
-
For an added bonus, I also discuss an unsolved problem
involving an Atari 2600 game,
Entombed
.
Just a heads up, this talk is
60-75 minutes long
. Concepts
will be discussed in great depth. However, the talk was
intentionally constructed for me to be over-prepared, with topics
that can be skipped if I do not have time to cover everything. As
such, I link to this page in the slides if anyone is interested in
the full talk. Audience interaction is welcome mid-talk. In the
event that I skip topics, the questions below are guaranteed to be
covered while I'm talking.
Questions
As a requirement, we had to put questions in for the audience to
answer on paper mid-talk. The answers were hidden in the slides to
see if students were paying attention. Here are mine, with answers
at the end of the page:
Given a 3D model
M
of
n
vertices, how many triangles are drawn if done via
Triangle List
?
What is lg
*
(2
2
65536
)? Alternatively, what is the lg
*
(
6
2)?
What does bitDP stand for?
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
Most graphs discussed in our Graph Theory are abstract and may be
visualised in any way as long as it follows a set of rules.
Likewise, in computer graphics, there are "rules" too. However,
they are quite different from the theoretical graph theory we are
used to discussing. How a vertex and an edge are percived are
different and absolute.
Here's a few rules:
Vertices have
positional
coordinates (x, y, z) to
define position in space. Consequently, this means that
there is only
one
way to represent them in space.
Edges (connections between vertices) are
implied
,
based on a drawing mode of the programmer's choice. They
all have their own advantages and disadvantages. I'll
go over them below.
Everything is oriented around
triangles
. Period. If
you wanted to make a square, you do it with two triangles.
If you wanted to make a curved surface, you have to
estimate it with triangles.
Coordinate Systems
We have three dimensions to work with here. The coordinates are
cartesian, and denoted with (x, y, z). Depending on implementation,
you may find the "y" axis being the "height" axis, or the "z" axis
being the "height" axis. For simplicity of this talk, any potential
discussion of 3D coordinates will assume "z" as the "height" axis.
This is shown as follows:

data.title: When Did Nature Burst into Vivid Color?
data.author: jandrewrogers
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了自然界中色彩和色觉的演化历史，提出了一个类似“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题：究竟是鲜艳的色彩信号先出现，还是识别这些色彩的色觉先演化出来？科学家Zachary Emberts和John Wiens通过研究化石记录和系统发育树，重建了5亿年的演化历史。他们发现，色彩信号和色觉可能是共同演化的。色彩信号用于吸引配偶、诱导传粉等，而色觉则帮助识别这些信号。尽管有些生物丧失了部分色觉能力，但色彩在演化过程中持续存在，表明其传递信息的益处超过了吸引捕食者的风险。文章还提到，像蜥蜴这样的动物通过色彩信号传递健康信息，而色彩和色觉的演化是一个复杂且相互关联的过程。

主要讨论点：颜色的演化及其在自然界中的作用

不同观点：
• antonvs引用《Calvin and Hobbes》来暗示对颜色和现实感知的讨论，但没有明确表达立场。

When Did Nature Burst Into Vivid Color?
By
Molly Herring
June 27, 2025
Scientists reconstructed 500 million years of evolutionary history to reveal which came first: colorful signals or the color vision needed to see them.

The natural world is awash with color, and many of these vibrant hues are meant to be seen. Apples blush red to coax animals to spread their seeds, lavender blooms are violet to lure in pollinating bees, and male peacocks trailed by flashy blue trains more successfully attract mates.
However, the world is colorful only for some of us. These vivid signals can be perceived by animals that can see in color; to organisms that have limited or no color vision, many of these bright colors don’t mean anything at all. This raises interesting evolutionary questions. Which came first: colorful signals or the color vision needed to see them? And when did these optical signals emerge and take off, painting the natural world in the kaleidoscopic spectrum we see today?
“Some birds are red, some snakes are red, and some plants have red fruits. In each of these cases, the red coloration serves as a signal,” said
Zachary Emberts
, an evolutionary biologist at Oklahoma State University. “This led us to wonder: What was the initial function of conspicuous coloration, like red, and color vision?”
Emberts and his former postdoctoral adviser
John Wiens
, an evolutionary ecologist at the University of Arizona, combed through research encompassing hundreds of millions of years of evolutionary history to offer a scientific answer to the
chicken-and-egg question of color
. The researchers used the fossil record and phylogenetic trees — timelines of species emergence that are based largely on modern traits — to infer when colorful signals may have first emerged in plants and animals. Then they tested their hypothesis that color vision and colorful signals evolved together.
“What I love about this paper is the ambition and confidence to pursue big questions and explore ideas that will inevitably involve speculation,” said
William Allen
, an ecologist who studies sensory systems at Swansea University in Wales and was not involved in the new study. “There is a tendency for science in the 21st century to focus on applying analytic techniques to data, and this can sometimes be at the detriment to deep thought, natural history and curiosity.”
The Evolution of Color
As a graduate student at the University of Texas, Austin, Wiens was fascinated by pretty animals. For his dissertation, he studied blue-bellied lizards, which have earth-toned backs and sapphire undersides, to examine how sexual signaling might have evolved. He built a phylogenetic tree of lizard species and was fascinated to see that the males’ blue patches, which signal fitness to females,
frequently disappeared and reappeared
along the evolutionary timeline, perhaps because females stopped picking up on the signals in some lineages. That project piqued his interest in how the production and recognition of color signals might have evolved.

As a graduate student, John Wiens first encountered colored patches used by lizards as a sexual signal. Decades later, he resumed his exploration of the use of color by organisms.
Ramona Walls
There are some costs to color. For example, a vivid signal to attract a mate may attract predators as well. But the persistence of color throughout evolutionary history suggests that, for many organisms, the information it communicates is beneficial enough to outweigh the cost. However, without color vision, the value of maintaining distinctive coloration would vanish; indeed, there would be little reason for it to evolve in the first place. That made Wiens wonder why different species evolved the ability to see color — perhaps to find colorful fruit, flowers or mates? Did those palettes even exist at the time?
Some components of color vision have been lost over evolutionary time.

data.title: All Good Editors Are Pirates: In Memory of Lewis H. Lapham
data.author: Caiero
data.article_summary: 这篇文章纪念了美国散文家兼编辑刘易斯·H·拉普姆（Lewis H. Lapham），他于2024年7月23日去世。作者聚焦于与刘易斯共事的时光，特别是拉普姆季刊（Lapham’s Quarterly）的创立过程。2007年，刘易斯在纽约曼哈顿创办该杂志，办公室里充满了书籍和知识的气息。作者作为首位全职编辑加入，见证了杂志从无到有，逐渐发展到拥有四万订阅者和年度盛会的过程。刘易斯工作勤奋，每期杂志的开篇文章都精心打磨，多次修改。他平易近人，乐于听取每个人的意见，尽管他出身名门，却常讽刺美国统治阶级。作者回忆起与刘易斯共度的时光，包括在酒吧讨论杂志内容和设计的夜晚，对他充满敬佩与怀念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Lewis Lapham的纪念及其相关话题的讨论，包括其作品、编辑理念以及创意与抄袭的界限。

不同观点：
• [skadamou] 分享了多个关于Lewis Lapham的悼念文章链接，引导读者去不同来源了解Lapham的生平和影响。
• [svara] 对Lapham的播客《The World in Time》给予高度评价，认为Lapham像是来自另一个时代的人物，强调其独特性。
• [PostOnce] 被文章顶部的图片吸引，引发对舞台设计模型和微缩模型的研究兴趣，偏离了原本对Lapham的讨论。
• [ggm] 提到Robertson Davies和E. Anne Proulx曾用小镇报纸编辑为主题进行写作，可能暗示Lapham的编辑风格与这些作家的文学主题有相似之处。
• [Aachen] 引用了文章中的一句话，指出Lapham认为“所有优秀的编辑都是海盗”，他们从每个人那里偷取灵感，以此解释编辑的创造性过程。
• [devrandoom] 讨论了灵感和抄袭之间的界限，认为虽然这条界限有时模糊，但确实存在。同时指出在创作过程中，借鉴主题是不可避免的，并以创作蓝调歌曲为例。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对Lapham作为编辑和创作者的角色有较多讨论，特别是他的“海盗”理念，即编辑需要从各种来源获取灵感，引发了对创意过程的深入探讨。
• 另外，部分评论如[PostOnce]偏离了对Lapham的直接讨论，转而关注文章附带的图像内容，显示出讨论的多样性和发散性。
• [devrandoom] 的评论特别指出了创意过程中的“偷取”和借鉴的必要性，并以具体例子说明，为讨论提供了实际论据。

This remembrance first appeared in
Stranger’s Guide
on July 28, 2024.
O
n July 23, 2024, the American essayist and editor Lewis H. Lapham died. Since then several beautiful obituaries have been written about the great man and I won’t attempt to repeat these, though I certainly encourage reading them. Instead I want to focus on a very particular time and place where I worked with Lewis and knew him best—the book-filled offices of his last great project,
Lapham’s Quarterly
.
After a storied tenure of nearly thirty years at
Harper’s Magazine
, Lewis founded
Lapham’s Quarterly
in 2007 as a magazine of the history of ideas. The offices were housed on Irving Place just off Union Square in Manhattan. Here I spent eight years as executive editor and found the offices to be a magical place filled with knowledge, wit, history, literature, and cigarette smoke. In those book-lined rooms I got an up-close lesson on how to start a magazine and how to run it with grace. It’s also where I met Abby Rapoport,
Stranger’s Guide
’s publisher and my co-founder as we built our own magazine years later.
Back in 2007 I was the first full-time editorial hire Lewis made. On my first day of work, I was greeted by the only other staff members in the office. The first was Ann Gollin, Lewis’ rock and longtime assistant. The second was a young intern in flip-flops and cut-off shorts. That was it, that was the entire operation. There was no website, no magazine, no subscribers. Instead there was just the beginning of Lewis’ idea that we cull through the great books and create a digest of thought and ideas. Each issue would be on a new theme, be it war, religion, or food.
When I left eight years later, Lewis had built a thriving magazine with forty thousand subscribers and an annual gala—the Decades Ball—headlined by the likes of Tom Hanks and Anne Hathaway. There was a robust intellectual editorial board that met four times a year around a large wooden table to discuss
Thucydides
,
Marx
, or
Hannah Arendt
.
But that all came later. On that very first day of work, Lewis took me out, first to a party at André Schiffrin’s penthouse apartment, where he introduced me to
Joan Didion
before slipping out to a late dinner at Elaine’s. Here we sat at what Lewis assured me was the best table in the house. Within minutes the grande dame herself, Elaine, plopped down at our table with a tremendous sigh, as if we were just the port in the storm she’d been waiting for. An endless stream of people dropped by to say hello or to drink or to argue politics late into the night. I was accustomed to a very different crowd—those of small leftist magazines and the New School philosophy graduate students.
“Where am I?” I wondered. “What have I just signed on to?”
When Lewis founded
Lapham’s Quarterly
, he had already been inducted into the American Society of Magazine Editors Hall of Fame. He was already famous as an essayist, editor, and author of countless books. But despite all his accolades, those early days at
Lapham’s Quarterly
had the feel of a 1940s movie about a plucky team of actors putting on a show, a kind of “Gee shucks folks, let’s make a magazine!” On Lewis’ desk, next to the ashtrays and the blue folders full of notes, sat the book
How to Start a Magazine
, which was hurriedly tucked away the day the
New York Times
came to photograph the offices. In those days, I was married to the magazine’s art director and we didn’t yet have kids. So almost every evening after work we’d head off for drinks with Lewis at the nearby bar, Paul & Jimmy’s, where Lewis quickly established himself as a regular. It was here we spent countless hours discussing this nascent publication, its cover, the printer, the feel of an issue, and ideas for themes and authors.
Lewis was an incessantly hard worker; he was the first to arrive at the office and the last to leave. Almost every night after work he’d head off to a dinner, a book party, or some other glamorous literary event. Although he was already in his seventies, I never saw a man work harder.
Each issue of
Lapham’s Quarterly
opened with an essay by Lewis that he would painstakingly labor over for weeks; seventeen drafts for one essay was not uncommon. Ann Gollin, his trusty accomplice in all things great and small, would diligently transcribe the essays he dictated on a small hand-held tape recorder. And then she’d transcribe them again, then yet again, as he crafted and re-crafted each sentence.
Lewis would show everyone in the office his drafts, from the interns to the publisher, asking eagerly, “What do you think?” He looked for ideas and input everywhere. He was never an elitist even though he summered in Newport, his pocket squares were crisp, and his cufflinks shined. Lewis’ essays poked fun at the American ruling class from his position within the belly of the beast.

• [ggm] 提到Robertson Davies和E. Anne Proulx曾用小镇报纸编辑为主题进行写作，可能暗示Lapham的编辑风格与这些作家的文学主题有相似之处。
• [Aachen] 引用了文章中的一句话，指出Lapham认为“所有优秀的编辑都是海盗”，他们从每个人那里偷取灵感，以此解释编辑的创造性过程。
• [devrandoom] 讨论了灵感和抄袭之间的界限，认为虽然这条界限有时模糊，但确实存在。同时指出在创作过程中，借鉴主题是不可避免的，并以创作蓝调歌曲为例。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对Lapham作为编辑和创作者的角色有较多讨论，特别是他的“海盗”理念，即编辑需要从各种来源获取灵感，引发了对创意过程的深入探讨。
• 另外，部分评论如[PostOnce]偏离了对Lapham的直接讨论，转而关注文章附带的图像内容，显示出讨论的多样性和发散性。
• [devrandoom] 的评论特别指出了创意过程中的“偷取”和借鉴的必要性，并以具体例子说明，为讨论提供了实际论据。

data.author: adocomplete
data.article_summary: 2025年7月1日，PlanetScale宣布推出私密预览版**PlanetScale for Postgres**，号称是全球最快的Postgres托管平台。该平台响应客户需求，旨在解决当前Postgres托管平台常见的宕机、性能差和成本高的问题。PlanetScale for Postgres使用真实Postgres运行于其专有操作器上，提供高可用性、自动故障转移、查询缓冲和连接池等功能，并支持无停机自动更新Postgres版本。此外，PlanetScale Metal的本地NVMe SSD驱动器显著改善了云中托管关系数据库的性能/成本比。虽然Vitess是PlanetScale的强项，但为了适应Postgres，正在从头构建新系统，未来将提供更多信息和早期访问机会。公司邀请运行大规模Postgres的企业参与合作。感兴趣者可注册私密预览等候名单。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PlanetScale 推出 PostgreSQL 服务的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• joshstrange：他从 PlanetScale 转向了 Neon，因为 PlanetScale 不支持每个租户一个数据库，而且需要为每个数据库支付高额费用。他的使用场景是小规模、自筹资金的公司，负载波动大但可预测。他认为 Neon 更适合他的需求，但仍然对 PlanetScale 抱有期待，并赞赏其产品和支持服务。

• kellysutton：作为一名使用 PlanetScale MySQL 两年的用户，他认为这是 PostgreSQL 社区的一个令人兴奋的消息。他将使用 PlanetScale 的体验比作从 Treo 手机升级到 iPhone，认为其在各个方面都更优秀，并祝贺 PlanetScale 团队。

• ezekg：他提到最近 PostgreSQL 的扩展和缩放技术发展，期待 PlanetScale 的进一步信息，并表示会持续关注。

• simonw：他关注 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 服务是否与 Vitess 有技术传承，并自行找到答案，确认这是从零开始构建的新系统。

• rtyu1120：他质疑为什么 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 在 Amazon EBS 上的表现被排除在基准测试之外，认为没有这一部分的基准测试显得不完整。

• samlambert：作为 PlanetScale 的代表，他表示团队在推出 PostgreSQL 产品过程中非常享受，并愿意回答任何问题。

• brycethornton：他认为更多/更好的竞争托管 PostgreSQL 服务是有益的，期待看到 Supabase 的 Multigres 与 PlanetScale 的对比。

• rodolphoarruda：他离题提到 PlanetScale 网站上的一个 MySQL 开发者课程，认为这是一个亮点。

• wasd：他祝贺 PlanetScale 的发布，并询问 PostgreSQL 扩展的可用性及其限制。

补充讨论：
• 技术传承和创新：simonw 和官方回应（samlambert）提到了 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 服务是从零开始构建的新系统，而非基于 Vitess 的技术。
• 竞争和对比：brycethornton 和 joshstrange 提到了与 Neon 和 Supabase 的竞争，并期待看到更多的对比和信息。
• 性能和基准测试：rtyu1120 质疑基准测试的完整性，特别是 Amazon EBS 部分的缺失。
• 功能和扩展性：wasd 和 ff4 关注 PostgreSQL 扩展的可用性及其在分布式系统中的表现和限制。

Announcing PlanetScale for Postgres
By
Sam Lambert
|
July 1, 2025
Today we are announcing the private preview of PlanetScale for Postgres: the worldâs fastest Postgres hosting platform.
You can request access to PlanetScale for Postgres by visiting this
link
.
We are already hosting customers' production workloads with incredible results.
Convex
, the complete backend solution for app developers, is migrating their reactive database infrastructure to PlanetScale for Postgres. Read more about their migration
here
.
Never say never
PlanetScale has been successful hosting some of the worldâs largest relational databases, so why are we building for Postgres? The reason is simple: customer demand. In March we announced
PlanetScale Metal
and something wild happened. We had an immense number of companies reaching out to us asking us to support Postgres. The demand was so overwhelming that by the end of launch day we knew we had to do this. We are nothing without our customers, we do the difficult but boring bit of providing industry leading uptime so they can build incredible products. We want more and more exciting companies building on PlanetScale.
Performance and reliability
Our initial goal was to convince ourselves we could be additive to the ecosystem and provide something of value. We spoke to over 50 customers of the current Postgres hosting platforms and we heard identical stories of regular outages, poor performance, and high cost. PlanetScale is an engineering company. We are not going to enter a market with anything but exceptional engineering.
We had to validate we could out-perform the current solutions while being more reliable. This led us to building a
comprehensive benchmark methodology
. After extensive testing we are proud to share that we consistently outperform every Postgres product on the market, even when giving the competition 2x the resources:
Amazon Aurora
AlloyDB
Lakebase/Neon
Supabase
Heroku
Crunchy Data
TigerData
PlanetScale for Postgres uses real Postgres running on our proprietary operator meaning we can bring the maturity of PlanetScale and the performance of Metal to an even wider audience. Todayâs release already achieves true high availability with automatic failovers, query buffering, and connection pooling via our proprietary proxy layer PSBouncer. We run Postgres v17 and support online imports from any version > Postgres v13, as well as automatic Postgres version updates without downtime. Additionally, PlanetScale Metalâs locally-attached NVMe SSD drives fundamentally change the performance/cost ratio for hosting relational databases in the cloud. Weâre excited to bring this performance to Postgres.
Vitess for Postgres
Vitess is one of PlanetScaleâs greatest strengths and has become synonymous with database scaling. Contemporary Vitess is the product of PlanetScaleâs experience running at extreme scale. We have made explicit sharding accessible to hundreds of thousands of users and it is time to bring this power to Postgres. We will not however be using Vitess to do this.
Vitessâ achievements are enabled by leveraging MySQLâs strengths and engineering around its weaknesses. To achieve Vitessâ power for Postgres we are architecting from first principles. We are well under way with building this new system and will be releasing more information and early access as we progress. As with all PlanetScale products we work with customers at scale to build and validate maturity. If your company runs Postgres at a significant scale and this is something that interests you,
reach out
.
We are incredibly excited to be a part of the vibrant and thriving Postgres community. Sign up for the private preview of PlanetScale for Postgres waitlist
here
.

主要讨论点：关于一篇论文中提出方法的实际应用和效果的讨论

不同观点：
• [sparacha] 作为论文的合著者，愿意回答有关其方法的任何问题，表现出开放讨论的态度。
• [pseudosavant] 关注该方法对请求延迟的影响，特别是通过代理时的延迟问题，暗示了对实际应用中性能的关心。
• [jgant13] 询问何时使用该方法而不是OpenRouter，显示出对不同工具选择标准的兴趣，特别是性能方面的比较。
• [tmaly] 提出关于模型量化的问题，关心在保持良好结果的前提下是否可以实现模型的量化。
• [_nh_] 要求与RouteLLM进行比较，显示出对该方法相对于其他类似工具的竞争力的关注。
• [jedisct1] 分享了实际使用体验，指出在特定任务（评级编码任务难度）中，该方法的表现不如Qwen2.5-Coder-7B，暗示了模型规模和性能之间的关系。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是该方法在实际应用中的性能表现，特别是在与其他工具和模型的比较中。
• 讨论还涉及模型的技术细节，如量化和规模对性能的影响，表明读者对实际部署中的技术实现细节有深入兴趣。
• 不同评论者根据各自的使用场景提出了具体问题和反馈，显示出对该方法在多样化应用场景中的实用性的关注。

data.title: Figma Files Registration Statement for Proposed Initial Public Offering
data.author: kualto
data.article_summary: Figma于2025年7月1日宣布，已向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交Form S-1注册声明，计划进行首次公开募股（IPO），发行A类普通股，并在纽约证券交易所上市，股票代码为“FIG”。目前，具体发行股数和价格区间尚未确定，发行将取决于市场条件。摩根士丹利、高盛、Allen & Company LLC和J.P. Morgan等将担任此次发行的主承销商。此前，Figma已于4月秘密提交了S-1草案。此次IPO尚需SEC批准，才能正式生效。Figma是一个帮助团队协作设计数字产品的平台，成立于2012年，现已发展为一个集成了AI功能的平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Figma的IPO及其背后的技术、商业和用户影响

不同观点：
• crossroadsguy认为，IPO通常标志着公司增长的顶峰，公众（散户投资者）可能成为最后的接盘者，难以在长期内获利。
• btown对Figma的技术成就和商业成功表示钦佩，强调其工程设计和产品优化是其成功的关键，并对团队的创新精神表示赞赏。
• Animats关注Figma的治理结构，尤其是CEO Dylan Field在IPO后仍将掌握大量投票权，这可能影响公司未来的决策。
• rco8786认为Figma的成功是一个启示，表明即使有现有解决方案，新创意仍有成功的机会。
• pm90对Figma在与Adobe竞争中幸存并成功IPO表示祝贺，带有一定的调侃意味。
• granzymes通过分析财务数据指出，Figma的收入增长显著，但运营支出和净收入表现不佳，暗示IPO可能是为了在增长放缓前套现。
• jonator将Figma的成功与Linear的故事相比较，强调通过简化和性能优化可以 disrupting 已有的市场参与者。
• lvl155认可Figma的产品质量，但对其在AI方面的策略表示担忧，认为应专注于增强设计师的能力，而非创建类似Dreamweaver的工具。
• greatgib认为Figma选择此时IPO是因为其意识到增长可能开始停滞，尤其是在AI图像编辑热潮带来的用户增长之后。
• Manik_agg回顾了Figma从阻止Adobe收购到如今IPO的历程，强调其独立发展的成就。
• lenerdenator讽刺地表示，在Figma开始为退休和养老基金支付时获得访问权，暗示对IPO后公司策略变化的不满。
• urda提到Figma曾通过法律手段打压竞争对手Loveable，对其商业行为提出质疑。
• StableAlkyne认为，公司上市通常对用户不利，尽管目前Figma是一个优秀的设计工具，但上市后可能会因股东压力而降低用户体验。

补充讨论：
• Figma的技术创新，尤其是其混合C++/JavaScript架构和WebGL渲染，被认为是其成功的关键因素。
• 财务数据展示了显著的收入增长，但也揭示了高运营支出和净亏损问题。
• 用户对IPO后公司策略变化的担忧，尤其是对产品方向和用户体验的影响。
• 对Figma治理结构中CEO集中投票权的关注，可能影响公司未来的决策和透明度。
• 对Figma商业行为的批评，特别是对竞争对手的法律行动，引发了对其商业伦理的讨论。

News
We’re sharing an update on Figma’s path to becoming a publicly traded company. After
submitting a confidential draft of our S-1
to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in April, it is now available to the public.
Figma, Inc. (“Figma”) today announced that it has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) relating to a proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock. Figma has applied to list its Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “
FIG
.”
The number of shares to be offered and the price range for the proposed offering have not yet been determined. The offering is subject to market conditions, and there can be no assurance as to whether or when the offering may be completed, or as to the actual size or terms of the offering.
The fine print:
Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Allen & Company LLC, and J.P. Morgan will act as joint lead book-running managers for the proposed offering. BofA Securities, Wells Fargo Securities, and RBC Capital Markets will act as book-running managers for the proposed offering. William Blair and Wolfe | Nomura Alliance will act as co-managers for the proposed offering.
The proposed offering will be made available only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the preliminary prospectus, when available, may be obtained from Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, New York 10014, or by email at prospectus@morganstanley.com; Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, New York 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; Allen & Company LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 711 Fifth Avenue, New York, New York 10022, by telephone at (212) 339-2220, or by email at allenprospectus@allenco.com; or J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, c/o Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, New York 11717 or by email at prospectus-eq_fi@jpmchase.com and postsalemanualrequests@broadridge.com.
A registration statement on Form S-1 relating to these securities has been filed with the SEC but has not yet become effective. These securities may not be sold, nor may offers to buy be accepted, prior to the time the registration statement becomes effective. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

data.title: Code⇄GUI bidirectional editing via LSP
data.author: jamesbvaughan
data.article_summary: 作者James B. Vaughan开发了一个概念验证系统，实现了现代代码编辑器与图形用户界面（GUI）之间的实时双向编辑。该系统通过语言服务器协议（LSP）实现，允许用户在首选代码编辑器（如Emacs）中编辑代码，同时自动更新GUI，反之亦然。这一概念在代码CAD系统中尤为实用。尽管双向编辑并非新概念，但与常用文本编辑器的实时双向编辑则是创新之处。现有的工具如Fusion 360和OpenSCAD仅部分实现此功能。作者希望这一演示能激发更多对LSP服务器创意应用的探索，并期待看到更多关于codeCAD的开发进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过双向编辑实现语义编辑、GUI操作及其实时反馈的工具和方法

不同观点：
• FloatArtifact认为双向编辑对于无障碍软件至关重要，尤其是在语音控制代码编辑和获取GUI元素方面，具有很高的实用价值。
• jasonjmcghee分享了自己在实时编码方面的实验，例如通过LSP实现实时更新运行程序，以及通过VS Code扩展实现滑块和颜色选择器等交互功能，表达了对这种技术的浓厚兴趣和探索精神。
• necovek指出使用LSP进行图形工作的参数化非常有用，并提到FreeCAD与Python绑定的经验，认为目前工具在编码与GUI之间切换的体验还不够流畅。
• mikewarot将当前技术与1990年代的Borland Delphi进行比较，强调了Pascal语言与GUI工具包的良好匹配性，同时也指出了C++等语言在GUI设计中的复杂性和局限性，期待LLMs能提高生产力。
• harrylepotter分享了在vscode中使用webviews进行类似操作的经验，指出在语言服务器与UI组件之间映射诊断信息的复杂性，并表示希望分享更详细的实现。
• rao-v讨论了CAD软件中的文件格式问题，指出目前缺乏能够捕捉设计概念的跨平台CAD文件格式，并提到OpenSCAD和STEP格式的局限性。
• williamcotton介绍了自己的项目，实现了GUI与shell管道的双向映射，并提供了截图和GIF说明。
• kennykartman提到fornjot这个CAD工具可能对相关需求有帮助，并对项目表示赞赏。
• ogoffart介绍了Slint GUI工具包及其LSP服务器，提供了在线演示，展示了通过LSP实现的实时预览和编辑功能。
• taeric回忆了自己对类似技术的兴奋，提到Minecraft的实时编码 session，表达了对这种技术的持续兴趣但尚未取得实质进展。
• junon表示即将开始类似的项目，开发以代码为核心的PCB编辑工具，认为当前讨论的技术是非常有价值的参考。
• rtcode_io分享了双向同步演示，特别是PDF方面的应用，展示了整个双向同步的实现。
• WillAdams提到曾建议在OpenPythonSCAD中实现类似的交互性，但担心细节问题会导致UI变得杂乱无章。
• pshc表达了对多模式协作编辑器的梦想，并鼓励继续努力。
• SwiftyBug对项目表示赞赏，并希望有人能在此基础上创建iOS应用的Interface Builder，以改善Xcode的糟糕体验。

补充讨论：
1. 讨论中多次提到LSP在双向编辑和实时反馈中的核心作用，以及其在不同领域（如代码编辑、GUI操作、CAD设计等）的广泛应用潜力。
2. 争议焦点在于当前工具在编码与GUI操作之间的切换体验不够流畅，以及文件格式和语言支持的局限性。
3. 多个参与者分享了个人项目和实验，展示了双向编辑和实时反馈技术的实际应用和可能性。
4. 讨论还涉及了历史技术（如Borland Delphi）与现代技术的比较，以及LLMs在提高生产力方面的潜力。

44435716.article_content:
Code⇄GUI bidirectional editing via LSP
Code⇄GUI bidirectional editing via LSP
Published:
2025-07-01T00:00:00Z
jamesbvaughan
https://jamesbvaughan.com/
July 1, 2025
I built a small proof-of-concept for a system that enables real-time
bidirectional editing between any modern code editor and a GUI, enabled by an
LSP
1
server.
Code-based CAD
I like working on small projects at home that benefit from CAD. I’m also a
programmer with a personal development environment that I’ve spent years making
as cozy as possible. Naturally I’ve been interested in finding code-based CAD
system to use for my projects that allows me to use that cozy development
environment.
I read
a recent update from Kevin Lynagh about his ongoing work on
codeCAD
,
and this part on bidirectional editing stood out to me (emphasis mine):
For example: One idea I’m exploring is “bidirectional editing”, so geometry can
be manipulated using either:
a purpose-built graphical UI, or
the textual codeCAD language
If you graphically drag a point around, the coordinates in the source code
should automatically update.
If you edit the source code, the graphical UI should automatically update.
A simple way to test this idea is to throw a
<textarea>
in the UI that
displays the corresponding source code.
But to me, that feels terrible because I never want to be coding in some janky,
in-browser
<textarea>
— I want to be working with source code in Emacs, with
all of my familiar key bindings, color schemes, autocomplete, and decades of
cozy practice.
That’s the core appeal of a textual programming language.
But doing this properly is an absolute boatload of work:
How does the system rewrite source code? Is it mediated by files on disk with
reload on save? How do the editor and UI stay in sync and avoid clobbering
each other’s unsaved changes?
Maybe we need an LSP server?
The language interpreter needs to preserve comments and flow them through,
even when the UI makes edits to the code.
What about whitespace / pretty-printing?
How much of this needs to be built to evaluate whether bidirectional editing
“fits nicely in the hand”?
In particular:
Maybe we need an LSP server?
I’ve been a happy user of LSP servers since they became commonplace in Neovim
setups
2
, but I have almost no experience with language server internals.
I had certainly never considered that they could facilitate bidirectional
editing with a GUI.
A proof-of-concept
That line from Kevin’s post was a proper nerd-snipe because a few hours later I
had built this proof-of-concept:
What you’re seeing here is a text editor next to a GUI, and data live-updating
both ways between them, made possible by a small server that uses LSP to
communicate with the text editor and WebSockets to communicate with a web app.
I’ve shared more technical details and the code for this demo
here on
GitHub
.
Why this excites me
Bidirectional editing isn’t new.
What’s new, as far as I’m aware, is real-time bidirectional editing
that works
with your favorite text editor.
I’ve tried out a handful of code-based CAD systems, but so far I haven’t found
any that achieve more than two out of these three features:
Real-time-ish updates in the GUI from changes made in the code
Real-time-ish updates in the code from changes made in the GUI
Works well with my preferred code editor
Fusion 360
has
decent bidirectional editing for parameters, but it’s not fully code-based and
it certainly doesn’t let me use my own editor.
OpenSCAD
doesn’t require the use of its own text
editor, and it’s possible to trigger reloads in the GUI via file watching
when you save source files in external editors, but it only goes one way.
Zoo
has some bidirectional editing, but only
with its built-in editor.
Arcol
, the tool that I help build at my day job
3
, is
innovating in CAD interface design in some exciting ways, but we’re building for
architects, not programmers.
This is just a toy demo, but it’s enough to excite me about the possibility of a
system that achieves
all three
of those points!
What’s next
I don’t plan to develop this demo further, at least not anytime soon, but I hope
it inspires people to find more creative uses (abuses?) of LSP servers.
One of the best code-CAD environments I’ve worked in is OpenSCAD + Neovim with
the
OpenSCAD LSP server
, only using
the OpenSCAD GUI for the viewer, not the built-in text editor.
OpenSCAD is fundamentally not built for GUI editing, but since it’s open source
and has a nice language server already, it could be a good place to develop a
more interesting demo of this concept.
Like Kevin’s post said, doing this properly will be a boatload of work.
Handling conflict resolution, incremental edits, and the more complex general
LSP server internals are all serious tasks, let alone creating a whole new
language for CAD.
I’m looking forward to seeing what Kevin comes up with for codeCAD!
LSP
is the
Language Server Protocol
.
It’s used by language servers to provide features like diagnostics, code
actions, go-to-definit
