The hidden JTAG in your Qualcomm/Snapdragon device’s USB port
Casey Connolly
Monday, June 30, 2025
9 min read
Please enter Mastodon Instance:
Submit
Cancel
Linux Kernel
Qualcomm
Back in February of this year, Qualcomm quietly published the source code for interacting with EUD. This is perhaps one of the most exciting things they’ve done lately - especially...
Back in February of this year, Qualcomm
quietly published the source code for interacting with EUD
. This is perhaps one of the most exciting things they’ve done lately - especially if you spend a lot of time debugging the kernel or U-Boot - let’s talk about it.
EUD stands for Embedded USB Debug: essentially, this is a debug interface built right into almost every Qualcomm SoC since ~2018. Internally it hooks deep into the SoC, providing debug facilities for not just the CPUs but also the myriad of Hexagon co-processor/DSPs; many of the exciting details can be found in
this patent from way back in 2014
.
In practise, for a non-production device (like a dev board, though some production devices seem to work too), EUD can be enabled by writing a few registers and then starting up the USB phy (though the details vary by generation). Instead of whatever typical gadget you might expect, what appears on your PC is a 7-port USB hub, with 1 port populated by the “EUD control interface”.
With the right USB commands, a second device will appear, this one exposes an SWD interface! Yes! SWD right over the USB cable, no external tools, no soldering, and no expensive debuggers. Closed case debug that (almost) puts Google’s Suzy-Q to shame!
For those unfamiliar: JTAG and SWD are both mechanisms for debugging the CPU cores inside a device, just like you can use GDB to debug programs on your computer (or your IDEs integrated debugger). They let you set breakpoints, halt execution, inspect the registers, single step instructions and all sorts of other useful things.
The code drop
For quite a while there has been a tantalising
fork of openOCD published by Qualcomm on CodeLinaro
, promising EUD integration. However, it relied on an at-the-time proprietary EUD library, which was only available to Qualcomm employees and their OEM partners.
The device-side part of this (enabling the EUD interface so it shows up on your PC) has been somewhat supported in upstream Linux for a while. Back in August last year there was an attempt to extend this support for some newer platforms which have additional requirements. This
sparked some discussion
over the kernel policy: is it acceptable to have drivers in Linux that are only usable by some internal software, gatekept for Qualcomm and their paying partners? The answer appeared to be no, and this seemed to be enough to push Qualcomm in the right direction as after 8 months of silence, here we are!
The code has finally dropped (
here’s the link again
), and they even updated their
openOCD branch
to point to the now open library, awesome!
Let’s try to use it…
src/swd_api.cpp:408:64: error: cast from 'std::nullptr_t' to 'uint32_t' {aka 'unsigned
int'} loses precision [-fpermissive]
408 |         queue_swd_packet_special(swd_handle_p, SWD_CMD_STATUS, (uint32_t)NULL,
&swd_status);`
Oh no.
Cleaning things up
Let’s be fair, it almost definitely builds just fine on Ubuntu 20.10 with Qualcomm’s GCC 8.x toolchain. But that’s not what most people are using, we have to fix this!
It turns out to be not too bad, just some minor stuff. Somehow they have
-Wall
and
-Werror
enabled though, and there is no way we’re gonna get that all passing just yet.
With everything building, the necessary fixes (and a shiny new
.gitignore
) have been submitted to Qualcomm’s repo
here
.
Now we have EUD building, we can try it with OpenOCD. It looks like they based their changes on the latest OpenOCD release 0.12.0, very nice. But wait, this release came out in 2023, and OpenOCD is still in active development… So there’s 2 years worth of changes, and
; git log --oneline v0.12.0 up/master | wc -l
10808
Almost 11k commits! It would really be nice to get this upstream eventually, so maybe let’s just rebase it real quick, we need to point it at the cleaned up EUD fork anyways.
Among Qualcomm’s changes to support EUD, there are also patches adding Hexagon debugging support (and seemingly some improvements for LLDB as well). These got lost along the way but are almost certainly worth looking into at some point.
So here we are, a fun day of fixing up and rebasing some codebases, and a very tasty reward!
; ./src/openocd -f tcl/interface/eud.cfg -f tcl/target/qualcomm/qcom.cfg

Licensed under GNU GPL v2
For bug reports, read
http://openocd.org/doc/doxygen/bugs.html

Info : Listening on port 4444 for telnet connections

data.article_summary: 这篇文章为网站管理员提供了关于创建有效链接文本的建议。主要要点包括：避免使用“点击这里”作为链接文本；链接文本应简短且有意义，提供上下文信息，解释链接内容，而不涉及技术细节或使用动词短语。例如，不要说“点击这里下载Amaya”或“前往Amaya网站下载软件”，而应直接使用“获取Amaya”。文章还提供了参考资料和示例，以帮助理解和应用这些建议。文章最后说明这些提示由W3C质量 assurance兴趣小组提供，是非规范性的参考信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：链接的最佳实践及其在用户体验（UX）、可访问性（accessibility）、搜索引擎优化（SEO）等方面的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持“点击这里”链接**：
   - crazygringo：认为“点击这里”非常清晰，能明确表示这是一个动作链接而非参考链接，特别是在下载或查找更多信息时。
   - orthoxerox：虽然“点击这里”不是最佳选择，但在强调动作链接时，它比信息性链接更有效，尤其是对不熟悉网页布局的用户。
   - johnisgood：支持“点击这里”直接链接最新版本，简化下载流程。

• **反对“点击这里”链接**：
   - robin_reala：从可访问性角度，认为“点击这里”对屏幕阅读器用户不友好，他们依赖链接列表进行导航，过多此类链接会破坏体验。
   - scary-size：引用英国政府数字服务指南，建议避免“点击这里”以提高可访问性。
   - rerdavies：认为“点击这里”和“告诉我更多”等表述不够优雅，建议直接链接目标内容。

• **支持描述性链接**：
   - retsibsi：倾向于使用描述性链接（如“Amaya网站”），能更明确地指示链接目的和内容。
   - seanwilson：强调描述性链接不仅有利于SEO，还可以通过额外文本或ARIA标签为屏幕阅读器提供更好的可访问性。
   - fkyoureadthedoc：支持简洁明了的链接格式，如[Download Amaya](http://link-to-file)，并建议使用下载图标以避免混淆。

• **个人偏好与风格**：
   - guhcampos：个人偏好名词作为链接，不喜欢使用动词或命令语气。
   - afandian：认为链接的形式（如下划线、按钮边框）与内容同等重要，当前趋势去除这些视觉提示可能导致用户困惑。

• **关于用户体验的讨论**：
   - jfax：提到一些用户缺乏网页垃圾过滤技能，可能误解链接文本，如“我忘记了密码”。
   - 1970-01-01：指出“点击这里”链接过短且易受附近链接干扰，尤其在触屏设备上。
   - t1234s：认为如果需要在UI中加入“点击这里”这样的指示，可能需要重新设计以提高直观性。

补充讨论：
• **可访问性与用户体验**：多个评论强调了可访问性在链接设计中的重要性，特别是对屏幕阅读器用户的考虑。
• **SEO与链接描述**：描述性链接不仅有助于用户理解，还能提升网页在搜索引擎中的可见性。
• **历史背景**：mmaunder提到此讨论曾对解决“点击这里”泛滥问题产生过影响，可能出现在Slashdot上。

争议焦点：
• **“点击这里”链接的清晰度与可访问性之间的权衡**：支持者认为其明确性高，反对者则认为其对屏幕阅读器用户不友好。
• **链接描述与动作指示的平衡**：如何在链接描述中有效传达动作（如下载）或内容（如更多信息）之间的最佳平衡。

Don't use "click here" as link text
What a link means
When calling the user to action, use brief but meaningful link text
that:
provides some information when read out of context
explains what the link offers
doesn't talk about mechanics
is not a verb phrase
An example
For instance, avoid the following sentence on your page:
To download W3C's editor/browser Amaya,
click
here
.
or:
To download Amaya, go to the
Amaya Website
and get
the necessary software.
Both of these sentences divulge too much of the mechanics of getting the
Amaya software. If you want to call your reader to action, use something
like:
Get
Amaya
!
Note that "get" is left out of the hypertext; we do not recommend putting
verb phrases in link text. Thus, rather than:
Tell me more
about Amaya.
You should write:
Tell me more about
Amaya
: W3C's free
editor/browser that lets you create
HTML
,
SVG
, and
MathML
documents.

section
6.1
Link text
in the W3C
HTML Techniques for Web
Content Accessibility Guidelines 1.0
, November 2000

about mechanics

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种针对高通Hexagon基带处理器的全系统模拟模糊测试工具。由于Hexagon架构的专有性，目前缺乏相关的安全工具，导致其成为安全研究的盲点。研究团队开发了首个开源工具链，利用QEMU的Hexagon全系统模拟分支与LibAFL结合，实现了对Hexagon固件的模糊测试。该工具链显著减少了工程工作量，并支持覆盖率引导的模糊测试，填补了Hexagon基带安全研究的空白。通过该工具，研究人员可以对iPhone等设备中的Hexagon基带进行分析，解决了缺乏完整系统模拟和专用工具的问题。研究团队已在TROOPERS25会议上发布了这一工具链，并邀请社区共同协作改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rizin工具对Hexagon ISA和MDT图像的支持及其在静态分析中的应用，以及对基带处理器安全性及市场现状的讨论。

不同观点：
• [xvilka]: 认为Rizin工具的`dev`版本对Hexagon ISA和MDT图像有良好的支持，并且RzIL的提升实现对静态分析有帮助。提供了相关实现的链接，供进一步参考。

• [jasonjayr]: 关注无线电频率（RF）方面的模糊测试（fuzz testing），尤其是基带处理器的RF端。提到软件定义无线电（SDR）让他意识到许多公开可访问的接口存在安全隐患，主要依赖于“必须接受有害干扰，且不应造成有害干扰”的规则。

• [le-mark]: 对基带处理器安全性表示担忧，提出这项工作是否会导致大量Qualcomm零日漏洞被发现。还质疑是否已有国家行为者先行探索过这些漏洞，而安全研究人员现在才开始追赶。

• [mschuster91]: 批评基带处理器市场的垄断现象，尤其是Qualcomm的主导地位。认为市场缺乏竞争，导致所有参与者都不重视代码质量和安全性。还提到进入该市场的难度，涉及复杂的标准和专利问题，甚至苹果公司也无法轻易取代Qualcomm和Broadcom。

补充讨论：
• [spr-alex]: 简单评价该工作为“非常好”。

• [meerasmatkhan]: 只提到“Tiktok”，与主要讨论点关系不大，可能是误解或无关评论。

争议焦点：
• 基带处理器市场的垄断问题以及由此导致的安全性不足，尤其是Qualcomm在市场中的主导地位及其影响。
• 关于Rizin工具在静态分析中实际效果的评价存在潜在讨论空间，尽管[xvilka]提供了具体实现链接以支持其观点。

44442189.article_content:
6/27/2025
Research by: Â
Bruno Produit, Luca Glockow, Rachna Shriwas
Hexagon fuzz: Full-system emulated fuzzing of Qualcomm basebands
Key takeaways
1. Due to Qualcommâs proprietary architecture, a lack of security tooling exists around their baseband
2. Our tooling enables research on Hexagon baseband with significantly reduced engineering work
3. We release the first open-source toolchain for full-system emulated Hexagon firmware fuzzing at
TROOPERS25
Overview
Every phone has a cellular baseband processor to handle mobile communications (5G, 4G, GPS, and more).
Qualcomm created a specific architecture for its baseband called Hexagon. It powers the baseband processors found in most leading smartphones, including every iPhone since generation 12 except iPhone 16e and all Snapdragon-based devices. This architecture, being different from the classic ARM, x86, or MIPS that we all know, leads to a lack of security research. Most of the produced tooling is simply not applicable to it!
We developed the first open-source toolchain for full-system emulated fuzzing of any Hexagon firmware. Our work addresses a gap in baseband security research by making a previously inaccessible attack surface available for analysis. With our toolchain, open-sourced
here
, we invite the community to collaborate and build upon this work.
Previous research landscape and the Hexagon gap
The baseband security research community has made considerable progress in recent years, yet a critical gap has persisted regarding Qualcommâs Hexagon architecture.
Early work like
BaseSAFE (2020, Maier and al.)
introduces an advanced framework for fuzzing basebands. Building on this,
FirmWire (2022, Hernandez et al.)
provides baseband emulation platforms for fuzzing.
These tools are the go-to solution for fuzzing basebands which use ARM, x86, MIPS and other standard architectures. But, as the FirmWire paper observes:
âUnlike other baseband implementations, Qualcomm leverages a fully-custom architecture known as Hexagon [â¦] Unfortunately, tooling for this architecture is sparse, and especially full-system emulators are lacking.â
Other research efforts around Hexagon are limited to specific aspects, such as DIAG protocol analysis and reverse engineering (see Figure 1).
Figure 1. Previous baseband research did not cover Hexagon baseband full system emulation
Challenges
Hexagon presents several barriers that make firmware analysis challenging:
Custom CPU architecture
: Most tooling lacks support, making reversing challenging
Custom OS and software stack
: Requires adapting common attack techniques
Custom communication protocols:
No free tools or documentation exist
The primary challenge in reversing Hexagon baseband lies in the lack of tooling support. Ghidra, IDA, and similar tools do not support the architecture out of the box, and while QEMU offers user-space emulation for Hexagon, full system emulation remains unavailable.
FirmWire, for example, relies on QEMU for emulation and introspection. Since Hexagon does not yet have proper full-system Hexagon emulation in QEMU, it is not possible to use it for analysing this firmware, as explained in the quote above.
Solution
To address these challenges, we used a QEMU fork from the Qualcomm Innovation Center (QuIC) supporting Hexagon full-system emulation. With the addition of LibAFLâs QEMU fork, we built a custom fuzzing and reverse engineering tool tailored for Hexagon.
â
1. How we merged QuIC/QEMU with LibAFLâs QEMU
The QEMU fork from QuIC includes a
hexagon_sysemu branch
that, with minor modifications, can successfully boot iPhone baseband firmware. We adapted this codebase for fuzzing by integrating it with
LibAFLâs QEMU
. Since the two projects share no common ancestor in Git, merging them requires significant manual effort and custom fixes.
We share our QEMU fork in
this
repository, which can be used directly. Like QuICâs fork, you can emulate Hexagon firmware and connect LLDB if you have Qualcommâs Hexagon SDK. You can also compile it as a library and connect LibAFL for introspection directly in Rust via its elegant API.
2. How we created a fully coverage-guided fuzzer
Using this approach, we can recreate something similar to FirmWire and use Rust-based hooks for control flow modification. When booting a baseband firmware, these code flow manipulations are necessary. The emulator wonât provide the hardware components that the firmware communicates with.
We created a fuzzer that handles control flow manipulation for a specific iPhone firmware, up to user mode, utilizing these LibAFL bindings. We provide this with a JSON-based approach, where you can set breakpoints with their handlers in the configuration. You can also modify the QEMU command line arguments to debug firmware emulation issues.
Figure 2. Snippet of the JSON-based configuration for Hexagon fuzz
With this tooling, a fully coverage-guided fuzzer can run on any Hexagon-based baseband firmware. This way, all the 5G/4G/GP

data.title: A proof-of-concept neural brain implant providing speech
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了加州大学戴维斯分校的科学家团队研发的一种新型神经假体，能够将脑信号直接转化为声音，实现实时语音交流。与以往将脑信号转化为文本的系统不同，该系统可以捕捉语音的细微差别，如音高和韵律，并以低延迟生成语音。过去此类系统存在延迟高、词汇有限以及无法处理非预设语言或名称等问题。团队通过256个微电极记录脑信号，并使用神经解码器和声码器合成语音。参与研究的ALS患者T15通过该系统实现了更自然流畅的交流。这项技术标志着向全数字化发声系统迈出了重要一步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：脑机接口设备的技术挑战、实际应用和未来潜力

不同观点：
• [x187463] 关注设备触发声音产生的机制，担心设备可能会无意中表达出用户不想公开的思维。这涉及到设备的激活机制以及与神经元的连接方式，用户对设备的控制程度是其主要关切点。

• [yaris] 对设备研发过程中所需的技术和设备来源感到好奇，质疑这些设备是外购还是内部自制，反映了公众对高科技设备研发过程的不了解以及对技术供应链的兴趣。

• [N_Lens] 认为神经-计算机接口，特别是电极技术，是当前发展的主要瓶颈。提出通过增加电极数量来突破瓶颈的常见方法，但也设想了非传统方法（如高保真合成神经纤维）作为潜在解决方案，显示出对技术创新的开放态度。

• [andrybak] 对研究成果的标题和宣传持批评态度，认为标题有误导性（点击诱饵），因为当前技术还不能实现清晰可懂的实时对话，强调目前只是概念验证阶段，而非成熟应用。

• [pingou] 展望了脑机接口技术的未来应用，包括“心灵感应”式的直接脑对脑通信，但也认识到信号转换和翻译的必要性，表现出对技术未来发展的乐观态度。

• [aitchnyu] 以幽默方式表达了对个人健康监测设备的需求，虽然内容偏向调侃，但也反映了公众对实用性强、个性化医疗设备的需求和期待。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的争议焦点之一是当前技术的成熟度和实际应用的可行性。例如，[andrybak] 对标题的批评表明了对夸大宣传的不满，而 [N_Lens] 则更关注技术实现的细节和潜在突破方向。
• 评论还显示出公众对脑机接口技术在伦理、隐私和控制方面的潜在问题的关注，如 [x187463] 对无意中表达思维的担忧。
• 不同评论者对技术未来发展的预期各异，从 [pingou] 的乐观展望到 [andrybak] 的谨慎态度，体现了对技术潜力的不同看法。

Stephen Hawking, a British physicist and arguably the most famous man suffering from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), communicated with the world using a sensor installed in his glasses. That sensor used tiny movements of a single muscle in his cheek to select characters on a screen. Once he typed a full sentence at a rate of roughly one word per minute, the text was synthesized into speech by a DECtalk TC01 synthesizer, which gave him his iconic, robotic voice.
But a lot has changed since Hawking died in 2018. Recent brain-computer-interface (BCI) devices have made it possible to translate neural activity directly into text and even speech. Unfortunately, these systems had significant latency, often limiting the user to a predefined vocabulary, and they did not handle nuances of spoken language like pitch or prosody. Now, a team of scientists at the University of California, Davis has built a neural prosthesis that can instantly translate brain signals into sounds—phonemes and words. It may be the first real step we have taken toward a fully digital vocal tract.
Text messaging
“Our main goal is creating a flexible speech neuroprosthesis that enables a patient with paralysis to speak as fluently as possible, managing their own cadence, and be more expressive by letting them modulate their intonation,” says Maitreyee Wairagkar, a neuroprosthetics researcher at UC Davis who led the study. Developing a prosthesis ticking all these boxes was an enormous challenge because it meant Wairagkar’s team had to solve nearly all the problems BCI-based communication solutions have faced in the past. And they had quite a lot of problems.
The first issue was moving beyond text—most successful neural prostheses developed so far have translated brain signals into text—the words a patient with an implanted prosthesis wanted to say simply appeared on a screen. Francis R. Willett led a team at Stanford University that
achieved
brain-to-text translation with around a 25 percent error rate. “When a woman with ALS was trying to speak, they could decode the words. Three out of four words were correct. That was super exciting but not enough for daily communication,” says Sergey Stavisky, a neuroscientist at UC Davis and a senior author of the study.
Delays and dictionaries
One year after the Stanford work, in 2024, Stavisky’s team
published
its own research on a brain-to-text system that bumped the accuracy to 97.5 percent. “Almost every word was correct, but communicating over text can be limiting, right?” Stavisky said. “Sometimes you want to use your voice. It allows you to make interjections, it makes it less likely other people interrupt you—you can sing, you can use words that aren’t in the dictionary.” But the most common approach to generating speech relied on synthesizing it from text, which led straight into another problem with BCI systems: very high latency.
In nearly all BCI speech aids, sentences appeared on a screen after a significant delay, long after the patient finished stringing the words together in their mind. The speech synthesis part usually happened after the text was ready, which caused even more delay. The latest system of this kind supported a dictionary of 125,000 words but it still failed when you tried to speak a different language or even say the unusual name of a café just around the corner.
So, Wairagkar designed her prosthesis to translate brain signals into sounds, not words—and do it in real time.
Extracting sound
The patient who agreed to participate in Wairagkar’s study was codenamed T15 and was a 46-year-old man suffering from ALS. “He is severely paralyzed and when he tries to speak, he is very difficult to understand. I’ve known him for several years, and when he speaks, I understand maybe 5 percent of what he’s saying,” says David M. Brandman, a neurosurgeon and co-author of the study. Before working with the UC Davis team, T15 communicated using a gyroscopic head mouse to control a cursor on a computer screen.
To use an early version of Stavisky’s brain-to-text system, the patient had 256 microelectrodes implanted into his ventral precentral gyrus, an area of the brain responsible for controlling vocal tract muscles.
For the new brain-to-speech system, Wairagkar and her colleagues relied on the same 256 electrodes. “We recorded neural activities from single neurons, which is the highest resolution of information we can get from our brain,” Wairagkar says. The signal registered by the electrodes was then sent to an AI algorithm called a neural decoder that deciphered those signals and extracted speech features such as pitch or voicing. In the next step, these features were fed into a vocoder, a speech synthesizing algorithm designed to sound like the voice that T15 had when he was still able to speak normally. data.title: Math.Pow(-1, 2) == -1 in Windows 11 Insider build
data.author: jai_
data.article_summary: 在Windows 11 Insider Preview的Canary频道（版本27881.1000）中，C#的`Math.Pow(-1, 2)`方法返回值为-1，而非预期的1。该问题由osu!游戏的一位用户报告，并在多个环境中得到验证，如C++的`std::pow(-1, 2)`也出现相同问题，而在Python中结果正确。该问题出现在使用.NET 8的VSCode中，配置为Windows 11 Insider Preview和.NET SDK 8.0.411。目前尚未确定回归原因和已知解决方案，问题尚未被归类和分配处理人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Math.Pow和std::pow函数在不同环境下的行为问题，以及该问题应如何处理和归责

不同观点：
• [Someone] 认为，作为错误报告者，不应被要求去验证和确保函数调用和输出的正确性，尤其是在.NET的动态特性下，验证过程并不简单。C#编译器的常量折叠或运行时编译方式可能导致问题，而这些问题可能在调用UCRT时才显现出来。
• [CodesInChaos] 对优化编译器没有将`pow`函数替换为更简单的`x * x`表示惊讶，并指出这种简单的平方操作应该在单元测试中覆盖。怀疑编译器优化可能导致问题在.NET中才暴露出来，因为JIT编译器可能没有C++编译器那么智能。
• [fn-mote] 关心这个问题是如何通过CI测试的，并对问题的责任归属（UCRT还是.NET）表示关注。
• [Aardwolf] 质疑操作系统和编译器之间的联系，认为Visual Studio的编译器和标准库版本不应与操作系统构建相关联，尤其是在Windows环境下。

补充讨论：

data.author: rain1
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要回顾了大型语言模型（LLM）的基础模型发展趋势，重点介绍模型大小和训练数据，不包含谣言或未证实的信息。文章提到：

1. **GPT-2系列（2019）**：包括1.37亿到16.1亿参数，训练数据集为WebText，约100亿token。
2. **GPT-3（2020）**：1,750亿参数，训练数据包括CommonCrawl、WebText2、Books1、Books2和Wikipedia，约4,000亿token，训练耗时数月，使用大量GPU。
3. **GPT-3.5和GPT-4（2022-2023）**：无官方架构或训练数据信息。
4. **Llama系列**：包括70亿到650亿参数，其中Llama 65B训练了1.4万亿token。Llama 405B（2024）模型通过高质量数据提升性能，但出现偏离纯文本生成引擎的趋势。
5. **Llama-4（2025）**：包含2万亿参数的MoE模型，但因学术不当行为引发信任危机，未正式发布。
6. **早期模型匮乏**：长时间没有与GPT-3相当的模型，直到405B模型发布成为转折点。

文章还指出，模型训练逐渐偏向优化基准性能，而非纯粹的文本生成。

主要讨论点：大型语言模型的数据压缩、性能表现、模型大小与硬件需求、以及相关技术细节的争议。

不同观点：
• **数据压缩的惊人程度**：[ljoshua] 对下载模型中压缩的大量数据表示惊叹，尤其是可以在无网络环境下使用。虽然模型并不完美，但能够在8.1 GB的文件中包含如此广泛的知识是令人印象深刻的。

• **模型大小与推理能力**：[mjburgess] 提到当前模型大小已经接近推理能力的收益递减点，进一步增加模型大小并未显著提升性能。未来的发展可能更多依赖于特定领域的专业化模型，并预计高质量的开源模型将需要约1TB的推理时间VRAM。

• **未提及的重要模型**：[kamranjon] 指出评论中忽略了Google的Gemma和Gemini系列模型，以及T5系列模型在迁移学习领域的开创性贡献。

• **大模型的兴趣与潜力**：[lukeschlather] 认为虽然大型语言模型受到关注，但最有力的前沿推理模型可能实际上比最大的公开模型要小。大型模型的发展可能已经进入收益递减阶段。

• **LLM作为压缩算法的讨论**：[angusturner] 反驳将LLM视为有损压缩的观点，提出LLM也是无损压缩算法，并提供了两个具体的无损压缩方法。

• **硬件需求与模型规模**：[dale_glass] 对模型大小与硬件需求的关系表示关注，询问如何将模型大小转换为计算机硬件需求，以及未来可能的硬件发展趋势。

• **合成数据的有效性**：[simonw] 反驳了对合成数据导致性能下降的普遍看法，指出AI实验室使用合成数据是因为它确实有助于训练更好的模型，并提到相关研究论文的支持。

补充讨论：
• **时间标注的奇怪性**：[unwind] 指出在标题中包含当前年份（"2025"）显得不寻常，给人一种寻找时间机器的错觉。

• **文章的错误与遗漏**：[christianqchung] 对原文的一些信息错误和缺少上下文表示不满，指出例如Llama 4 Maverick和Behemoth的混淆，以及遗漏了Mistral large等重要模型。还提到模型训练和推理所需的GPU资源问题。

争议焦点：
• 大型语言模型的数据压缩特性及其是否应被视为有损或无损压缩。
• 合成数据在模型训练中的有效性及其可能导致的问题。
• 模型大小与推理能力之间的关系，以及未来模型发展的方向。

总结：讨论主要围绕大型语言模型的数据压缩能力、硬件需求、合成数据的使用及其性能表现展开，不同观点对模型当前状态及未来发展方向提出了各自的见解和质疑。

base model trends.md
How large are large language models? (2025)
This aims to be factual information about the size of large language models. None of this document was written by AI. I do not include any information from leaks or rumors. The focus of this document is on base models (the raw text continuation engines, not 'helpful chatbot/assistants'). This is a view from a few years ago to today of one very tiny fraction of the larger LLM story that's happening.
History
GPT-2,-medium,-large,-xl
(2019): 137M, 380M, 812M, 1.61B. Source:
openai-community/gpt2
. Trained on the unreleased
WebText
dataset said to 40GB of Internet text - I estimate that to be roughly 10B tokens. You can see a list of the websites that went into that data set here
domains.txt
.
GPT-3 aka davinci, davinci-002
(2020): 175B parameters. There is a good breakdown of how those parameters are 'spent' here
How does GPT-3 spend its 175B parameters?
. Trained on around 400B tokens composed of CommonCrawl, WebText2, Books1, Books2 and Wikipedia. Source
Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
. These training runs required months of a data center full of tens of thousands of A100 GPUs
source
.
GPT-3.5, GPT-4
(2022, 2023): No official factual information on architecture or training data available.
Llama
*
Llama 7B, 13B, 33B, 65B
: The 65B model was pretrained on a 1.4T (trillion tokens) dataset. LLaMA was officially stated to use Books3
source
as a data set - this is a very important dataset which has been pivotal in lawmaking regarding the training of AIs on large amounts of copyrighted and potentially pirated material.
Llama-3.1 405B
(2024): The 405B llama model was released. This is a dense transformer model, meaning all parameters are used in inference passes. Initial pretraining: 2.87T tokens, long context: 800B, annealing: 40M - so 3.67T total. source:
The Llama 3 Herd of Models
. By this point meta has learned to say less about what data goes into the models
"We create our dataset for language model pre-training from a variety of data sources containing knowledge"
- so I can't say as much about what goes into the training data here.
Empirically, we find that annealing (see Section 3.4.3) on small amounts of high-quality code and mathematical data can boost the performance of pre-trained models on key benchmarks
The emerging trend of
annealing
pretrained models to 'benchmax' is unfortunate in that it biases the base language models somewhat away from being pure text continuation engines. This should really be part of the post-training which aims to make the models role play as some kind of AI-chatbot helpful assistant character. But these companies care very much about metrics and scores.
Llama-4
(2025): The largest in the llama4 family is a 2T total parameter MoE model - A288B 16E (active 288B parameters, 16 Experts).
It is unreleased
. As for the smaller llama4 models (which are distilled from the large one): There was a scandal as facebook decided to mislead people by gaming the lmarena benchmark site - they served one version of llama4 maverick there and released a different version of llama4 maverick, for some reason. This academic misconduct led to reduced trust in the llama team which seems to have imploded shortly after. It's unclear if the 2T Behemoth model will ever be released after what happened. The smaller LLama4 models (maverick and scout), are distilled off this large one, and are generally considered to be of low-intelligence.
The desert
For a long time, there weren't really any
large
language models available to download. There was certainly nothing comparable with GPT-3 for a few years. There were projects to try to match it, but generally they operated by fine tuning things like small (70B) llama models on a bunch of GPT-3 generated texts (synthetic data - which can result in degeneration when AI outputs are fed back into AI training intputs).
The release of 405B was a turning point here. Just before

data.title: Jack Welch, the Man Who Broke Capitalism (2022)
data.author: throw0101b
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了杰克·韦尔奇（Jack Welch）在通用电气（GE）担任CEO期间（1981-2001）对资本主义的影响。作者大卫·盖勒斯（David Gelles）在新书《打破资本主义的人》（The Man Who Broke Capitalism）中指出，韦尔奇通过裁员、外包、收购和股票回购等方式，专注于最大化股东价值，使这一模式成为美国商业的常态。这种做法加剧了社会经济不平等，并损害了许多采用这种模式的公司。

文章还提到，韦尔奇的影响延伸至波音公司。自1997年起，几位曾受教于韦尔奇的CEO试图将波音转型为更像GE的公司，导致公司文化从航空工程转向金融工程。这种转变使得波音在737 Max客机事件中，工程师和试飞员在做安全决策时优先考虑股票价格，最终导致严重后果。文章认为，韦尔奇的遗产对现代企业管理造成了深远的负面影响。

David Gelles has been reporting on American CEOs for years at The New York Times. But there’s one CEO who stands heads and shoulders above his peers. He’s been retired for more than two decades, but his impact is still felt. Revered by some and reviled by others, his name is Jack Welch and he served as the CEO for General Electric (GE) from 1981 to 2001.
In Gelles’ new book, The Man Who Broke Capitalism:
How Jack Welch Gutted the Heartland and Crushed the Soul of Corporate America―and How to Undo His Legacy
, he chronicles how Welch’s laser focus on maximizing shareholder value by any means necessary - including layoffs, outsourcing, offshoring, acquisitions, and buybacks - became the new playbook in American business. The book demonstrates how this shareholder maximizing version of capitalism has led to the greatest socioeconomic inequality since the Great Depression and harmed many of the very companies that have embraced it.
I recently discussed the book with Mr. Gelles. The interview was condensed and edited for clarity. If you’re interested in viewing a video of the entire discussion,
click here

Soul of Corporate America—and How to Undo His Legacy
Simon & Schuster
Why do Americans revere our CEOs so much? Why does Jack Welch stand out among the crowd?
To get at the root of why this society seems to put our bosses up on pedestals, look back well over 100 years to the way we celebrated some of the early industrialists who rose to such great heights. We have the same veneration for modern-day technologists and entrepreneurs who are able to create amazing new breakthroughs and products.

In a big, diverse country that never had a monarchy or a unified religion, and is increasingly polarized and fractured, we look to our business leaders as some of the most important and perhaps some of the last sort of cultural touchstones who can be relevant to society at large. This helps explain some of the reasons we have some of the problems we do today.
I argue in the book that Jack Welch was a celebrity CEO. He was trying to marry this American reverence of CEOs with the modern media ecosystem, and he used it to disastrous effect. It was only through our collective veneration of Welch that he was able to be so influential over such a long period.
In the book, you draw a line from Jack Welch to the 737 Max issues at Boeing. Can you walk me through that?
Starting in 2019, I was one of the reporters at the
New York Times
who started digging into Boeing after the second crash of the 737 Max. The plane’s technical problem was very clear early on. There was a bad piece of software that relied on one flimsy sensor on the fuselage of the plane. So, we understood, in theory, what caused the planes to crash.
What we started understanding as we dug deeper, though, was that there was a cultural story. Over 25 years, something fundamental had shifted inside Boeing—the company’s priorities and what made it tick. When we started trying to understand that cultural change, it was a story of Jack Welch.
Starting in 1997, three successive CEOs who studied at Jack's knee at GE, took over Boeing. They deliberately, explicitly tried to make Boeing more like GE. And in doing so, they transformed one of the great American manufacturers, a company that for nearly 100 years had been focused on aeronautical engineering, into one that was motivated by financial engineering.
Records from congressional inquiries revealed messages between mid-level Boeing employees. These records showed that engineers and test pilots were thinking about the stock price when making decisions about safety. The awareness of the company's stock price percolated all the way down to the level of people who should be focused on the quality and safety of the plane, not Wall Street.
In 2011, Boeing faced this critical juncture; it was faced with the loss of a major order from American Airlines. The company had been a Boeing customer for decades, so they gave the Boeing CEO, Jim McNerney, a courtesy call to let him know that they were about to place a big order from Airbus instead of Boeing. McNerney asked for a week or two to make a counter-offer. In those few days, Boeing decided to redesign the 737 one more time. data.title: Performance Debugging with LLVM-mca: Simulating the CPU
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍如何使用LLVM的性能分析工具llvm-mca调试和优化ARM NEON矢量化的卷积内核代码。文章首先提到两个即将举办的矢量化工作坊，然后以一个简单的C语言卷积核为例，展示如何将其外层循环矢量化以提升性能。通过使用ARM NEON指令，如`vld1q_f32`和`vmlaq_laneq_f32`，作者对代码进行了优化，并尝试通过减少内存加载次数进一步提升性能。然而，优化后的代码运行速度反而变慢。作者使用llvm-mca工具分析发现，尽管减少了加载指令，但其他指令的延迟导致性能下降。最终，作者通过具体案例演示了如何使用llvm-mca来深入分析和调试性能问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLVM-MCA工具的局限性和使用体验

不同观点：
• Pornel认为LLVM-MCA工具潜力大，但在实际代码优化中存在限制。他指出该工具的问题包括：仅支持最内层循环的连续指令，无法处理函数的设置/拆解成本，不支持分支比较，且无法直接用于比较不同版本的代码。他提到在比较有无分支的算法版本时，需要手动删除分支，这增加了工作量并可能影响分析结果。此外，不同版本的代码可能有不同的循环展开次数或每次迭代处理不同数量的元素，导致需要手动重新调整度量标准。总体而言，他认为这对于优化高层次的C或Rust代码来说非常费力且效果不佳。

• Camel-cdr则关注LLVM-MCA中处理器调度模型的准确性问题。他指出并非所有处理器都使用自己的调度模型，不同模型的准确性各有差异。例如，Cortex-A72、Cortex-A76和Cortex-A78都使用Cortex-A57模型。此外，neoverse系列中的V1模型具有15的issue宽度，而V2和V3则为6。这表明不同处理器的模型选择和配置可能对工具的分析结果产生影响。

补充讨论：
• Pornel的观点更侧重于工具在实际代码优化中的使用体验和功能局限性，特别是手动操作和比较不同代码版本时的困难。
• Camel-cdr则关注工具在不同处理器架构下的技术细节和潜在的不准确性，强调了不同处理器模型之间的差异对工具分析的影响。

争议焦点：LLVM-MCA工具在处理分支比较和不同处理器模型支持方面的局限性以及如何改进以提升实用性和准确性。

data.title: Off with Their Heads: Illustrations of Blemmyes (ca. 1175–1724)
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了历史和传说中的无头人部落“Blemmyes”或“Akephaloi”，其形象出现在公元前4世纪的希罗多德著作中，描述其眼睛和嘴巴长在胸部。这种无头人也在中世纪的旅行文学和动物寓言中频繁出现，如《约翰·曼德维尔游记》和《亚历山大传奇》。尽管这些生物从未真正存在，但它们的形象在不同历史时期和地域被不断重塑，从恐怖的战士到奇异的幻想生物，甚至在16世纪的探险文献如《圭亚那的发现》中再次被提及。这些描述反映了古代和中世纪人们对未知世界和奇异生物的想象。

主要讨论点：对Umberto Eco的小说《Baudolino》的评价，特别关注历史与幻想元素的结合以及其影视化潜力。

• [comrade1234] 认为《Baudolino》前半部分的历史描写（如北意大利战争、德国皇帝巴巴罗萨、十字军东征和君士坦丁堡等）更吸引人，并从中获得了对意大利历史的深入理解。该读者对历史部分的欣赏超过后半部分的奇幻冒险，尤其提到书中描述的家族建造塔楼互相攻击的细节，以及城市被摧毁的可能性，让他对历史有了更深的认识。

Off with Their Heads: Illustrations of Blemmyes (ca. 1175–1724)
Miniature from a 14th-century manuscript of
The Travels of Sir John Mandeville
.
Before we “lost our cool”, we “lost our heads”. The latter idiom dates back to the eighteenth century, but the literal phrase from which it stems (read: decapitation) was in use since at least the time of Chaucer. Long before English existed as a language, however, a headless tribe was thought to roam the distant reaches of the world. They were known variously as Blemmyes or Akephaloi, and later discovered again in the New World as Ewaipanoma. It wasn’t that this species lacked a face. The eyes, nose, and mouth were all present on their chest. Where the brain supposedly resided. . . well that’s lost to history.
The earliest known reference to headless men comes from the Greek historian Herodotus, during a discussion of the eastern region of Libya in the fourth century BCE. “In that country are the huge snakes, and the elephants and bears and asps, the horned asses, the dog-headed men and the headless that have their eyes in their breasts, as the Libyans say”. Pliny the Elder offered a parallel account in his
Natural History
, describing a people who “have no heads, their mouths and eyes being seated in their breasts”.
No matter that a headless tribe of people never existed, their inclusion in ancient histories made them popular fodder for later bestiary and travelogue traditions. Beginning with their appearance in the late-tenth century
Marvels of the East
, the Blemmyes often look just as confused as we are — staring out at the viewer, as if trying to understand where, exactly, their neck went wrong. In these illustrations, Blemmyes frequently keep equally strange bedfellows. The thirteenth-century
Rutland Psalter
illustrates a headless archer aiming an arrow at some kind of merman who plays the trumpet with his butt; a circa 1475 manuscript of the
Miroir Historial
has a Blemmye cavorting with a dog-faced friend and a man with a tongue like an elephant’s trunk; an illustration from Giovanni Battista de’ Cavalieri’s 1585 monster book shows a Blemmye in the midst of regretting what he wished for: he finally has a head and a neck, but it is grafted from an enraged swan. Sometimes they are terrifying, wielding clubs and crossbows, and other times unexpectedly cute, such as in a sixteenth-century copy of Zakariya al-Qazwini’s
The Wonders of Creatures and the Marvels of Creation
(1280), where an orange Blemmye looks embarrassed for the bipedal jackals that dance above his missing head.

The inclusion of Blemmyes in the
Alexander Romance
spawned a subtradition all its own. In a fifth-century Armenian variation of the tale, translated by Albert M. Wolohojian, they are remembered as a rather gregarious, seafood-loving people.
Moving on, we came to a place where there were headless men. They had no heads at all, but had their eyes and their mouths on their chests, and they talked with their tongues like men. They were hairy and dressed in skins, a fish-eating sea people. And they gathered there, on land and from the sea,
hydna
, which we have at home. They got twenty-five liters worth and gave them to us. And we saw many huge sea lions slithering on the ground. And we saw, too, lobsters as big as ships.
In the mid-fourteenth century
Travels of Sir John Mandeville
, the Blemmyes seem to have migrated, from Africa to the Andaman Islands. The narrator describes seeing “ugly folk without heads, who have eyes in each shoulder; their mouths are round, like a horseshoe, in the middle of their chest” as well as “headless men whose eyes are mouths are on their backs”.
The Blemmyes were resurrected yet again during the Age of Exploration. In the
Discovery of Guiana
(1596), Sir Walter Raleigh reports rumors about the existence of men called Ewaipanoma: “folk of foul stature and of cursed kind that have no heads.
44410464.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了历史和传说中的无头人部落“Blemmyes”或“Akephaloi”，其形象出现在公元前4世纪的希罗多德著作中，描述其眼睛和嘴巴长在胸部。这种无头人也在中世纪的旅行文学和动物寓言中频繁出现，如《约翰·曼德维尔游记》和《亚历山大传奇》。尽管这些生物从未真正存在，但它们的形象在不同历史时期和地域被不断重塑，从恐怖的战士到奇异的幻想生物，甚至在16世纪的探险文献如《圭亚那的发现》中再次被提及。这些描述反映了古代和中世纪人们对未知世界和奇异生物的想象。

不同观点：

data.title: PortablE
data.author: BruceEel
data.article_summary: Portabl E是AmigaE编程语言的改进版，旨在实现跨平台兼容。最新版本r6b支持AmigaOS4、AROS、MorphOS，并为AmigaOS3、Linux和Windows提供不同程度的支持。提供多种示例代码、截图及预编译程序。下载时需输入用户名"user"和密码"password"以防止机器人滥用带宽。文档和手册可在作者网站查阅，另有论坛、邮件列表等支持渠道。作者还提供了AmigaE的初学者指南及对C++的批评文章。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amiga E 编程语言中的"but"操作符的用途及其独特性

不同观点：
• postexitus认为Amiga E中的"but"操作符不常见，虽然记得其语法，但一直不理解其具体用途。他提到自己曾经以为这是Amiga领先于其他竞争对手的一个特点，因为其他系统使用的是C或D语言。这暗示他认为"but"操作符可能是Amiga独有或先进的特性，但其具体作用不明确。

• 一些回复者（从链接中推测）解释了"but"操作符的实际用途。根据提供的链接内容，"but"操作符用于执行一个语句，但返回另一个值。例如，它可以用于在执行一个副作用的同时，保留另一个表达式的值。这表明"but"操作符实际上是一种语法糖，旨在提供更灵活的编程方式，但可能在实际使用中不太直观。

补充讨论：
• postexitus的编辑补充确认了他的记忆是正确的，并提供了进一步的参考链接（https://cshandley.co.uk/JasonHulance/beginner_93.html）。这表明他通过查找外部资料验证了自己的记忆，并且该链接可能对其他有相似疑问的人有帮助。

• 争议焦点在于"but"操作符的实用性和理解难度。对于不熟悉Amiga E的程序员来说，这种操作符的语义和用途可能显得不直观，从而引发对其存在价值的疑问。然而，对于熟悉该语言的用户，它可能提供了一种简洁的表达方式。

• 总体来看，讨论反映了对特定编程语言特性的记忆和理解之间的差距，以及通过外部资源验证和澄清的过程。

data.title: Ask HN: Why there is no demand for my SaaS when competition is killing it?
data.author: drvroom
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何将SaaS产品销售给中小企业和大型企业，以及在销售过程中遇到的挑战和策略。

不同观点：
• **Mekoka的观点**：认为向大型企业销售SaaS时，需要针对有决策权的人，并提出不仅要销售工具，还要提供解决问题的服务，成为“魔术师”来吸引客户注意。
• **Bitbasher的观点**：强调时机和精准营销，建议通过社交媒体监控客户的痛点，并通过提供付费产品试用而不是“免费试用”来吸引客户。同时，强调快速响应和从取消订阅的客户那里获取反馈的重要性。
• **Jwr的观点**：指出市场营销变得更为重要和困难，传统广告效果不佳，内容营销也因SEO和AI生成内容的泛滥而变得更具挑战性。
• **Codingdave的观点**：认为客户只关心“更多价值”如果它能解决更多问题，建议通过与客户沟通来了解他们的痛点并调整产品价值主张。
• **Pradeepodela的观点**：分享了自己在产品推广中遇到的流量和目标用户不匹配的问题，并指出即使产品好，如果没有足够的曝光也难以成功。
• **Vlod的观点**：质疑产品是否经过客户验证，建议首先要确保产品对客户当前的工作流程有明显改善，否则即使产品再好也难以销售。
• **Jameslk的观点**：区分了自上而下和自下而上的销售策略，指出针对不同层次的客户需要不同的销售和营销方法，强调关系和早期验证的重要性。
• **Bko的观点**：认为直接销售是唯一有效的方法，建议通过与客户直接沟通来了解他们的问题，而不是直接推销产品。
• **Kjksf的观点**：指出提供具体的网站和营销材料对于给出具体建议至关重要，强调细节决定成败。
• **Wiradikusuma的观点**：分享了自己通过个人关系获得付费客户的经验，并对教科书式的数字营销效果表示怀疑。
• **Throwawayffffas的观点**：建议通过现实世界中的会面来展示产品，并认为面对面的交流能获得更真实的反馈。
• **Jpc0的观点**：认为如果连自己都不相信产品，那就无法成功销售，强调自信心的重要性。
• **Franze的观点**：简单直接地问是否已经有一个付费客户，暗示获取第一个付费客户是关键步骤。
• **Sakerbos的观点**：强调利用自己的人脉网络，认为通过口碑可以获得更多的付费客户。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：如何有效销售SaaS产品，特别是在大型企业和中小企业的不同策略上，以及数字营销与个人关系在销售中的相对重要性。
• **重要论据和例子**：
  - Mekoka提到提供服务以解决客户问题。
  - Bitbasher分享了通过社交媒体监控和快速响应获得客户的经验。
  - Jwr指出传统广告和内容营销的困难。
  - Pradeepodela强调流量和目标用户匹配的重要性。
  - Vlod质疑产品是否经过客户验证。
  - Jameslk详细描述了自上而下和自下而上的销售策略。
  - Bko强调直接销售和与客户沟通的重要性。
  - Kjksf指出具体细节对给出建议的重要性。
  - Wiradikusuma通过个人关系获得付费客户的经验。
  - Throwawayffffas建议通过面对面的会面获得反馈。
  - Jpc0强调自信心对销售成功的重要性。
  - Franze和sakerbos都认为获得第一个付费客户是关键。

这些观点和例子为销售SaaS产品提供了多种策略和思考角度，特别是针对不同类型客户和市场环境的适应性。

data.title: Spain and Brazil push global action to tax the super-rich and curb inequality
data.author: Traces
data.article_summary: 西班牙和巴西在联合国发展融资会议期间发起了一项联合倡议，呼吁全球对超级富豪征收更高税收，以解决不平等问题。该倡议指出，最富有的人往往通过合法漏洞和较低税率支付较少的税，而普通纳税人负担更重。两国提议加强政府间信息共享，改善数据质量，识别和堵住税收漏洞，甚至考虑建立全球财富登记系统。倡议还包括技术合作和培训，以加强国家税收系统。该行动旨在推动全球税收更加透明、公平，并实现可持续发展目标。G20国家此前已在2024年达成类似协议，此次倡议进一步推动对高净值人群的税收改革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何解决财富不平等以及对富人征税的可行性和后果

不同观点：
• [支持对富人征税]  
  - 观点：对富人征税是拯救经济和社会的唯一途径。富人囤积财富导致经济活动减少，财富集中在少数人手中，普通民众无法参与经济活动。通过征税，政府可以刺激经济活动，增加就业，提供公共服务。  
  - 论据：历史上曾有过类似做法，如"新政"（New Deal）。高收入人群有较高的储蓄倾向，而低收入人群则有较高的消费倾向，因此对富人征税可以促进经济活力。

• [自动化和技术进步加剧不平等]  
  - 观点：自动化和人工智能的发展加剧了财富不平等，低技术含量的工作逐渐被取代，劳动价值下降，美国梦变得越来越不现实。  
  - 论据：技术进步使得普通劳动者的收入增长受限，财富不平等问题在民主制度下可能难以解决，因为富有的少数群体有强大的影响力。

• [税收制度不公平]  
  - 观点：当前的税收制度对中高收入者不公平，特别是在一些国家如西班牙，收入低于30万欧元的人承担了较高的税负。  
  - 论据：需要一个合理的税收制度，确保公平，而不是仅仅对富人征税。

• [鼓励投资而非征税]  
  - 观点：超级富豪通过投资保持财富，应通过减少官僚程序和障碍来鼓励投资，而不是增加税收。  
  - 论据：财富不平等本身不是问题，问题在于教育和机会的不平等，以及进入市场的障碍。

• [具体国家案例和政策]  
  - 观点：德国的财富税自1997年以来被暂停，因为计算方法过时且被认为违宪。

44441855.article_content:
Spain and Brazil push global action to tax the super-rich and curb inequality
1 July 2025
Economic Development
Spain and Brazil have launched a joint initiative to promote higher tax contributions from the super-rich worldwide, aimed at tackling soaring inequality by ensuring those with the most pay their fair share.
Presented during the UN’s
4th International Conference on Financing for Development
– taking place this week in Sevilla, Spain – the proposal highlights a growing problem: the richest individuals often contribute less to public finances than ordinary taxpayers, thanks to lower effective tax rates and legal loopholes.
“Our countries need more and more public revenues to meet their needs. Inequality is a problem everywhere and
the richest pay less than the middle class – even less than lower-income taxpayers
,” said Spain’s Secretary of State for Finance Jesús Gascón, during a press conference at the conference venue, where temperatures have soared to record highs in recent days.
The two governments are calling on others to join a drive for a fairer, more progressive global tax system. They point to a stark reality: the wealthiest one per cent of the global population owns more than 95 per cent of humanity combined.
UN News/Matt Wells
The Spanish Secretary of State for Finance Jesús Gascón (on screen) addresses a meeting at the Financing for Development conference in Sevilla, Spain.
Sharing knowledge, closing gaps
In today’s interconnected world access to reliable data is essential. The initiative prioritises information sharing - between governments and tax authorities – to help expose gaps in tax systems, close loopholes and combat evasion and avoidance.
Improving data quality and building national capacities for data analysis will help tax administrations identify where and how wealth is concentrated, how much is currently being paid and what needs to change.
Though some progress has already been made, the countries say much more must be done and many more countries should come on board.
“
There’s a real need to know who the beneficial owners are behind companies and legal structures used to conceal wealth
,” said Mr. Gascón. The initiative also proposes technical cooperation, training in data analytics and peer review mechanisms to strengthen national tax systems.
A global wealth registry?
Spain and Brazil are even considering steps toward a global wealth registry – acknowledging that this would take time, political will and major national efforts.
But the aim is clear: more transparency, more accountability and fairer contributions from the richest.
“
We cannot tolerate the intensity of inequality, which has been increasing in recent years
,” said Brazil’s Minister-Counsellor to the UN, José Gilberto Scandiucci denying that this was some kind of far-leftist agenda.
“
This is a moderate initiative to confront a very radical reality
.”
The proposal forms part of the
Seville Platform for Action
, which is turbocharging voluntary actions to help reach the
Sustainable Development Goals
(SDGs) – currently way off track for the 2030 deadline.
G20 highlights 'high worth' factor
It also follows the 2024 agreement by the G20 industrialised nations who met in Rio (Brazil) last year – the first international accord to commit to a joint tax agenda for high-net-worth individuals.
A three-month work plan is now being drawn up with regular meetings planned to track progress. The goal – bring more countries, international organisations and civil society on board to push forward tax reforms targeting the ultra-rich.
“If we want to effectively tax the super-rich, fight inequality and make our tax systems fairer and more progressive,
we need political will – and we need to act within our means
,” Mr. Gascón added.

data.title: They tried Made in the USA – it was too expensive for their customers
data.author: petethomas
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国国内生产与进口产品之间的成本、价格和生产能力平衡，以及关税政策的影响。

不同观点：
• **Strict9**：认为只有当生产规模扩大、基础设施增加、成本下降后情况才会改善。中国具有快速扩大生产线的能力，而美国已经失去了这种能力。关税不能解决问题，小规模实验也大多会失败，消费者最终会承担成本。

• **GlibMonkeyDeath**：指出即使零售商不愿提高价格，国内商品价格仍会上涨，且消费者最终会承担关税成本。以沃尔玛为例，指出即使大公司也无法承受供应链成本大幅上升的压力。

• **aeonik**：提到一些国内生产实验项目，如SmarterEveryday的尝试，尽管面临挑战，但仍有一些消费者愿意购买高价商品。

• **hammock**：通过Tuft and Needle的例子，说明一些公司最初在国内生产独特产品，但后来转向进口以降低成本，失去独特性。

• **PaulHoule**：回顾历史，指出纺织制造业早已外移，美国本土在制造业上的竞争力早已丧失。

• **rayiner**：对比1980年代与现在，指出当时国内服装生产比例高，但并未导致生活水平下降，质疑如今依赖国外廉价商品是否真正有利。

• **xiphias2**：认为美国过度依赖中国进口是不明智的地缘政治决策，应在多国间保持平衡。

• **giantg2**：质疑以昂贵的利基产品为例是否具有代表性，希望看到更多普遍商品的例子。

• **MangoToupe**：认为资本主义市场应自行解决问题，没有必要特别支持美国制造，消费者应根据市场选择产品。

• **thotghig5896**：指出低价进口商品降低了消费品价格，虽然导致美国经济依赖他国，但限制进口会导致经济困境。

• **k__**：认为美国难以在价格上竞争，但可以通过创新和新解决方案在某些领域取得优势。

• **netfl0**：不支持国内生产低端产品如塑料狗床。

• **fnordpiglet**：回顾制造业外流历史，指出美国自身生产质量下降也是原因之一，全球化只是加速了这一趋势。建议美国应发挥自身优势，而非试图恢复过去。

• **superultra**：质疑是否应在国内恢复重工业生产，指出工业劳动对环境和工人健康的长期负面影响。

• **v5v3**：建议不必所有产品都国内生产，可以仅在国内生产高端产品线，以满足不同消费群体的需求。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于是否应通过关税和国内生产来保护和促进美国制造业，以及消费者是否应为高价国内产品买单。
- 历史背景和全球化对美国制造业的影响被多次提及，尤其是生产能力和质量的变化。
- 讨论中涉及到国内生产的环境和健康代价，以及市场机制在解决这些问题中的作用。

data.title: Cloudflare to introduce pay-per-crawl for AI bots
data.author: scotchmi_st
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为“按爬取付费”（Pay per Crawl）的新方案，旨在让内容创作者对人工智能爬虫访问其内容有更多控制权。当前，内容创作者面临两个选择：完全开放或完全封锁内容访问。然而，许多出版商和内容创作者希望能通过让AI爬虫付费来获取内容访问权限。Cloudflare推出的“按爬取付费”功能允许内容所有者设置统一的收费标准，决定是否允许、收费或阻止特定爬虫访问。该系统利用HTTP 402状态码和Web Bot Auth技术确保安全和验证，同时让出版商在现有安全策略基础上灵活控制访问权限和定价。该功能目前处于私人测试阶段。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare 提出的通过支付进行网页爬取的方案及其争议

不同观点：
• **支持支付爬取的立场**（asim）：asim 认为 Cloudflare 的方案为微支付提供了一种解决方案，类似于 Coinbase 引入的 x402 库。该立场支持通过支付来减少爬虫对网站的负担，并提供了一种可能的实现方式。

• **批评与替代方案建议**（JimDabell）：JimDabell 认为 Cloudflare 的方案没有为额外成本提供价值，只是简单要求支付。他建议通过共享基础设施来减少重复爬取，并认为应该有一个协作的爬虫系统，而非各自独立爬取。他还指出，支付机制未必能有效解决问题。

• **进一步改进建议**（asimpletune）：asimpletune 支持支付爬取的方向，但认为应该根据用途收费，比如研究用途可免费，商业用途则应高收费。他提出理想的世界图书馆模式，但也承认目前不可行。

• **垄断与商业利益考虑**（mattlondon）：mattlondon 认为 Google 等大公司已经通过流量交换获得了爬取的优势，而其他公司爬取内容则没有回报。因此，Cloudflare 的方案对小公司和内容所有者有利，并可能增加其客户群。

• **广泛应用的潜力**（vasilzhigilei）：vasilzhigilei 认为 Cloudflare 的方案具有巨大潜力，尤其是如果扩展到所有客户。博客所有者等可能从中受益。

• **去中心化的担忧**（Zenul_Abidin）：Zenul_Abidin 认为应该考虑去中心化的支付方案，如Chromium曾提出的Web Monetization API，以避免依赖单一供应商。

• **对互联网未来的担忧**（skenderbeu, nottorp）：skenderbeu 担心付费浏览的趋势会导致互联网封闭，nottorp 则质疑 Cloudflare 未来是否会像过去的公司一样变得普遍不受欢迎。

• **竞争影响的顾虑**（Toritori12, saddlerustle）：Toritori12 认为大公司如Google可能不受此方案影响，从而继续免费爬取。saddlerustle 则建议开发一个开放协议来处理爬取权限和支付问题，而非依赖 Cloudflare。

• **技术和道德考量**（1dom, adjfasn47573）：1dom 认为 Cloudflare 的方案会强化其在互联网中的地位，不利于去中心化和自托管。adjfasn47573 则认为互联网的变革不可避免，AI可能带来更少广告和更多真实信息的未来。

• **特殊用途的考虑**（FloatArtifact）：FloatArtifact 提出对于使用AI爬虫作为无障碍工具的用户，应该有特殊考虑，以避免验证机制带来的不便。

补充讨论：
• **支付爬取的实际操作性**：讨论中多次提到如何有效实施支付爬取，包括如何定价、如何避免小网站失去流量、以及如何处理大公司的垄断问题。
• **去中心化与开放协议的需求**：多个评论提到需要一个去中心化和开放的协议来处理爬取和支付问题，以避免依赖单一供应商。
• **互联网变革的不可避免性**：有评论认为互联网的变革是必然的，AI可能带来积极的变化。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare 方案的实际效果和公平性，尤其是对大公司和小网站的不同影响。
• 去中心化与供应商依赖的问题。
• 支付爬取是否会带来互联网的封闭和不公平竞争。

44432385.article_content:
Introducing pay per crawl: enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers for access
2025-07-01
Will Allen
Simon Newton
5 min read
A changing landscape of consumptionÂ
Many publishers, content creators and website owners currently feel like they have a binary choice â either leave the front door wide open for AI to consume everything they create, or create their own walled garden. But what if there was another way?
At Cloudflare, we started from a simple principle: we wanted content creators to have control over who accesses their work. If a creator wants to block all AI crawlers from their content, they should be able to do so. If a creator wants to allow some or all AI crawlers full access to their content for free, they should be able to do that, too. Creators should be in the driverâs seat.
After hundreds of conversations with news organizations, publishers, and large-scale social media platforms, we heard a consistent desire for a third path: Theyâd like to allow AI crawlers to access their content, but theyâd like to get compensated. Currently, that requires knowing the right individual and striking a one-off deal, which is an insurmountable challenge if you donât have scale and leverage.Â
What if I could charge a crawler?Â
We believe your choice need not be binary â there should be a third, more nuanced option:
You can charge for access.
Instead of a blanket block or uncompensated open access, we want to empower content owners to monetize their content at Internet scale.
Weâre excited to help dust off a mostly forgotten piece of the web:
HTTP response code 402
.
Introducing pay per crawl
Pay per crawl
, in private beta, is our first experiment in this area.Â
Pay per crawl integrates with existing web infrastructure, leveraging HTTP status codes and established authentication mechanisms to create a framework for paid content access.Â
Each time an AI crawler requests content, they either present payment intent via request headers for successful access (
HTTP response code 200
), or receive a
402 Payment Required
response with pricing. Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record for pay per crawl and also provides the underlying technical infrastructure.
Publisher controls and pricing
Pay per crawl grants domain owners full control over their monetization strategy. They can define a flat, per-request price across their entire site. Publishers will then have three distinct options for a crawler:
Allow:
Grant the crawler free access to content.
Charge:
Require payment at the configured, domain-wide price.
Block:
Deny access entirely, with no option to pay.
An important mechanism here is that even if a crawler doesnât have a billing relationship with Cloudflare, and thus couldnât be charged for access, a publisher can still choose to âchargeâ them. This is the functional equivalent of a network level block (an HTTP
403 Forbidden
response where no content is returned) â but with the added benefit of telling the crawler there could be a relationship in the future.Â
While publishers currently can define a flat price across their entire site, they retain the flexibility to bypass charges for specific crawlers as needed. This is particularly helpful if you want to allow a certain crawler through for free, or if you want to negotiate and execute a content partnership outside the pay per crawl feature.Â
To ensure integration with each publisherâs existing security posture, Cloudflare enforces Allow or Charge decisions via a rules engine that operates only after existing WAF policies and bot management or bot blocking features have been applied.
Payment headers and access
As we were building the system, we knew we had to solve an incredibly important technical challenge: ensuring we could charge a specific crawler, but prevent anyone from spoofing that crawler. Thankfully, thereâs a way to do this using
Web Bot Auth
proposals.
For crawlers,
this involves:
Generating an Ed25519 key pair, and making the
JWK
-formatted public key available in a hosted directory
Registering with Cloudflare to provide the URL of your key directory and user agent information.
Configuring your crawler to use
HTTP Message Signatures
with each request.
Once registration is accepted, crawler requests should always include
signature-agent
,
signature-input
, and
signature
headers to identify your crawler and discover paid resources.

44432385.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为“按爬取付费”（Pay per Crawl）的新方案，旨在让内容创作者对人工智能爬虫访问其内容有更多控制权。当前，内容创作者面临两个选择：完全开放或完全封锁内容访问。然而，许多出版商和内容创作者希望能通过让AI爬虫付费来获取内容访问权限。Cloudflare推出的“按爬取付费”功能允许内容所有者设置统一的收费标准，决定是否允许、收费或阻止特定爬虫访问。该系统利用HTTP 402状态码和Web Bot Auth技术确保安全和验证，同时让出版商在现有安全策略基础上灵活控制访问权限和定价。该功能目前处于私人测试阶段。
44432385.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare 提出的通过支付进行网页爬取的方案及其争议

不同观点：
• **支持支付爬取的立场**（asim）：asim 认为 Cloudflare 的方案为微支付提供了一种解决方案，类似于 Coinbase 引入的 x402 库。该立场支持通过支付来减少爬虫对网站的负担，并提供了一种可能的实现方式。

• **批评与替代方案建议**（JimDabell）：JimDabell 认为 Cloudflare 的方案没有为额外成本提供价值，只是简单要求支付。他建议通过共享基础设施来减少重复爬取，并认为应该有一个协作的爬虫系统，而非各自独立爬取。他还指出，支付机制未必能有效解决问题。

• **进一步改进建议**（asimpletune）：asimpletune 支持支付爬取的方向，但认为应该根据用途收费，比如研究用途可免费，商业用途则应高收费。他提出理想的世界图书馆模式，但也承认目前不可行。

• **垄断与商业利益考虑**（mattlondon）：mattlondon 认为 Google 等大公司已经通过流量交换获得了爬取的优势，而其他公司爬取内容则没有回报。因此，Cloudflare 的方案对小公司和内容所有者有利，并可能增加其客户群。

• **广泛应用的潜力**（vasilzhigilei）：vasilzhigilei 认为 Cloudflare 的方案具有巨大潜力，尤其是如果扩展到所有客户。博客所有者等可能从中受益。

• **去中心化的担忧**（Zenul_Abidin）：Zenul_Abidin 认为应该考虑去中心化的支付方案，如Chromium曾提出的Web Monetization API，以避免依赖单一供应商。

• **对互联网未来的担忧**（skenderbeu, nottorp）：skenderbeu 担心付费浏览的趋势会导致互联网封闭，nottorp 则质疑 Cloudflare 未来是否会像过去的公司一样变得普遍不受欢迎。

• **竞争影响的顾虑**（Toritori12, saddlerustle）：Toritori12 认为大公司如Google可能不受此方案影响，从而继续免费爬取。saddlerustle 则建议开发一个开放协议来处理爬取权限和支付问题，而非依赖 Cloudflare。

• **技术和道德考量**（1dom, adjfasn47573）：1dom 认为 Cloudflare 的方案会强化其在互联网中的地位，不利于去中心化和自托管。adjfasn47573 则认为互联网的变革不可避免，AI可能带来更少广告和更多真实信息的未来。

• **特殊用途的考虑**（FloatArtifact）：FloatArtifact 提出对于使用AI爬虫作为无障碍工具的用户，应该有特殊考虑，以避免验证机制带来的不便。

补充讨论：
• **支付爬取的实际操作性**：讨论中多次提到如何有效实施支付爬取，包括如何定价、如何避免小网站失去流量、以及如何处理大公司的垄断问题。
• **去中心化与开放协议的需求**：多个评论提到需要一个去中心化和开放的协议来处理爬取和支付问题，以避免依赖单一供应商。
• **互联网变革的不可避免性**：有评论认为互联网的变革是必然的，AI可能带来积极的变化。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare 方案的实际效果和公平性，尤其是对大公司和小网站的不同影响。
• 去中心化与供应商依赖的问题。
• 支付爬取是否会带来互联网的封闭和不公平竞争。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者对收集到的数千个益智药（nootropics）评分的分析。益智药广义上指任何声称能提升认知能力的物质，包括处方药、植物、少量娱乐药物以及像睡眠和锻炼等活动。由于个体差异，益智药的效果因人而异。作者开发了一个推荐系统，用户输入自己尝试过的益智药评分，系统会推荐可能适合他们的其他益智药。作者收集了1981人的29,387个评分，加上之前的数据共36,163个评分。评分采用0-10的尺度，0代表完全无效或副作用过大，1-4代表可能有效果，5-9代表明显效果，10代表改变生活。分析中考虑了缺乏随机分配、自我报告偏差和缺乏控制与盲法等偏见。这些评分帮助预测某个人对特定益智药的潜在反应，但需注意结果可能受到 placebo 效应的影响。所有数据和代码均公开。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：有关益智药（nootropics）的有效性和安全性讨论

不同观点：
• **益智药与自然活动的对比**：
   - **negativepanda**：认为简单的益智药如咖啡加上自然散步比单独做一件事效果更好，且这种组合能带来期待感。
   - **reverendsteveii**：通过每天20分钟的阻力训练和有氧运动，得到了显著的益智效果，并认为运动是改变生活的“益智药”。

• **益智药效果的持久性与副作用**：
   - **icameron**：基于个人经验，认为益智药在初期效果明显，但随着时间推移，大脑会适应，效果减弱，甚至可能产生副作用，最终适得其反。例如SNRIs和Kratom都出现了类似的问题。
   - **butlike**：指出像安非他明这样的药物可能带来的改变未必是正面的，暗指其潜在的负面影响。

• **对益智药讨论的信任问题**：
   - **taeric**：认为由于缺乏大规模随机试验，益智药的讨论充满不确定性，尤其在自己使用Adderall的情况下，更加难以信任这些讨论。
   - **cckolon**：质疑个人经验的说服力，认为如果没有盲法试验，很难确定效果是否为安慰剂效应。

• **特定物质的讨论**：
   - **gavinray**：认为Modafinil、Racetams、Phenibut等物质效果明显，但Noopept未被提及，表示困惑。
   - **wslh**：强调某些物质如安非他明对大脑功能有直接且不可逆的影响，需给予强烈警告，与Omega-3等其他物质形成对比。

• **运动作为益智药的讨论**：
   - **Workaccount2**：强调运动的重要性，批评许多人抱怨健康问题却不愿尝试运动。
   - **Analemma_**：总结认为，除ADHD药物外，大多数益智药效果有限，而运动尤其是重量训练和高强度间歇训练（HIIT）具有显著益智效果，这符合进化视角。

补充讨论：
• **益智药的文化与信息来源**：
   - **readthenotes1**：提到益智药社区和初学者指南，并指出一些信息中的拼写错误，反映出对益智药讨论中的信息质量问题。

• **外部资源与数据支持**：
   - **runamuck**：提到Scott Alexander的益智药调查和分析，提供了一个外部资源以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 益智药的长期效果与副作用：个人经验显示益智药初期有效，但随着时间推移效果减弱并可能产生副作用，这与运动等自然方式的持久效果形成对比。
• 对益智药讨论的信任度：缺乏大规模试验导致对益智药效果的信任问题，尤其是在涉及药物如Adderall的情况下。

总结：评论围绕益智药的有效性、副作用、自然活动的替代效果以及对益智药讨论的信任问题展开，强调了运动作为一种有效的益智方式，并对某些药物的长期效果和潜在风险提出了警告。

Home
About

What I learned gathering thousands of nootropic ratings
March 23, 2022
tags:
nootropics
,
data-analysis
Credit: Ultra Heaven
In this post, I analyze nootropics ratings I gathered through a
recommender system
. Jump directly to
What I learned
if you don’t like caveats and methodology.
INTRODUCTION
#
What is a nootropic?
I will use the term
nootropic
as broadly as possible to describe
“Any substance purported to increase or enhance cognitive abilities."
Some only use the term
nootropic
to refer to a specific thing which should check a
very specific checklist
, e.g. having very few side-effects. As I’m not using this definition,
remember that the
nootropics
mentioned here can be very dangerous
.
This includes prescribed medications, plants, recreational drugs in small quantities, and more (I even included activities like sleep or exercise). If you hadn’t heard of “nootropics” before, you should also know that some people like to experiment with them and share their experience on communities like the
nootropics subreddit
, which has a great
begginer’s guide
.
The effectiveness of a nootropic varies a lot from one person to another (
your mileage will vary
). This is why I built a
nootropic recommendation system
Enter ratings on nootropics you’ve tried, and it will spit out nootropics liked by people with similar rating patterns. This was initially based on the
2016 SlateStarCodex nootropics survey
data.
, which I suggest you try before reading this post.
Still, it is helpful to understand how good each nootropic is in general, if only to prioritize further research. Indeed, my cunning plan with this recommendation system was to incentivize people to answer a boring survey. My plan worked better than I expected, and I got 1981 people to enter 29,387 nootropic ratings
Adding to it the original SlateStarCodex data, we have 36,163 ratings from 2,802 people.
, which I analyse in this post. Thanks everybody!
All data and code can be found
here
.
RATINGS
#
People interested in the code or the details of the analysis can look at
the RMarkdown notebook
.
How to interpret these ratings
#
Scale
#
I used the scale from
SlateStarCodex nootropics surveys
, which is:
0 means a substance was totally useless, or had so many side effects you couldn’t continue taking it.
1 - 4 means subtle effects, maybe placebo but still useful.
5 - 9 means strong effects, definitely not placebo.
10 means life-changing.
Ok but why?
I mostly used this scale so I could use SSC data when launching my recommendation system, but let me try to defend it. When someone tries a nootropic, either it seems to work, and the person will continue taking it, or it doesn’t seem to work, and the person will quickly stop taking it. This means we should expect people to have more certainty about nootropics that seem to work at least a little than on nootropics that don’t seem to work. If we want to compress a user experience into a 1D number, it makes sense to allow a more fine-grained judgment on positive nootropics
Why not make a scale from -10 to 10 then? Well, I just stole the scale, you know, but I think people really hate entering fine-grained ratings when they don’t have enough information.
. An issue is that this doesn’t differentiate between “Doesn’t do anything” and “I cannot feel my left arm anymore after trying this nootropic”. I tried to remedy this by asking people about the issues they had. Another issue is that some people might not read the scale description and think below 5 is negative and above is positive. I tried to take this into account in my analysis.
Biases
#
In order of importance (I think):
Lack of random allocation
The people who entered their rating on my recommender system were not randomly assigned to try specific nootropics. Thus we can expect a (usually positive) correlation between “I’m likely to try nootropic A” and “Nootropic A might work on me”.
This means that my estimations don’t represent the ratings a random person would get on average (which would usually be lower); they’re instead a prediction of the rating that a person would give to a nootropic if they decided to take it organically. Take this into account when transferring the results to yourself.
Self-report
You take a pill. It makes you feel good. You go on a website which asks you how good the pill is. You say it’s awesome. Little did you know that it was, in fact, merely good.
Take this into account when reading these ratings, especially if improving your mood is not your main goal.
Lack of control and blinding
Relatedly, these uncontrolled and unblinded ratings are partly driven by the placebo effect.
The sophisticated objection would be that this is probably less of a problem than for normal medications. The
placebo effect seems to be in large part due to regression to the mean
(when you’re sick, you’ll likely get better with time, not worse), which should not be an issue for nootropics in most cases. But the placebo effect does seem to be r

Alberto Fortin是一位有15年经验的软件工程师，他分享了使用大型语言模型（LLM）的实际体验。最初，他对LLM充满热情，希望其能革新开发流程，但在使用Go和ClickHouse重建基础设施时遇到许多问题。他的博客和后续分析指出，AI的宣传与现实存在差距，尽管新模型如Claude Opus 4有所改进，但仍未完全解决核心问题。

Alberto强调，LLM在初期使用时看似能大幅提升生产力，但实际上在处理复杂生产代码时经常出现错误，导致开发者需要耗费更多时间修复。他建议开发者应将LLM视为辅助工具，而非主导，保持对代码库的完全掌控。最终，他呼吁理性看待AI技术，既要利用其优势，也要认识到其局限性，找到平衡的使用方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **LLMs在生成代码方面的局限性**：[x187463] 认为LLMs生成的代码缺乏开发者的认知参与，管理这些代码很困难，尤其在需要长期维护的项目中。LLMs更适合一次性脚本或短期项目。
• **LLMs可能降低生产力**：[stephendause] 指出LLMs有时会因为提供错误信息而让用户走上错误的路径，浪费时间。虽然总体上LLMs是有帮助的，但需要用户检查其来源。
• **LLMs如类固醇，效果与副作用并存**：[noisy_boy] 将LLMs比作类固醇，认为其能快速提高生产力，但副作用明显，例如编程能力的退化。
• **LLMs忽视简单而重要的设计原则**：[jimbokun] 认为LLMs容易生成复杂的、难以重构和理解的代码，而忽视了将复杂问题分解为简单组件的重要性。
• **LLMs作为代码审查和概念解释工具**：[seanw444] 和[Const-me] 都将LLMs用作个性化的、快速的知识获取工具，而不是完整的代码生成器。Const-me还提到LLMs在代码审查中的作用，尽管需要筛选其建议。

补充讨论：
• **LLMs的局限性和特定领域表现不佳**：[quaintdev] 分享了LLMs在解决特定技术问题时的不足，例如无法提供最佳解决方案。
• **LLMs是新的速成方案现象**：[andy99] 认为LLMs是一种新的快速解决方案潮流，但现实中并没有真正的捷径，只有权衡和取舍。
• **LLMs在不同工作流中的应用**：[jjice] 和[hedgehog] 都提到LLMs在减少重复性工作方面的优势，例如生成模板代码和测试。同时，他们也强调了提示词优化和代码审查的重要性。
• **LLMs信仰与实际效果的争议**：[obirunda] 指出了对LLMs效果的信仰差异，一些人认为LLMs能大幅提高生产力，而另一些人则对其效果持怀疑态度。
• **LLMs未来发展的可能性**：[kadhirvelm] 提出了LLMs作为编译器的未来可能性，认为未来可能无需直接关注代码，而只需关注功能特性。

争议焦点：
• LLMs在编程中的实际效果和长期影响：一些人认为LLMs能显著提高生产力，而另一些人则担心其副作用和对开发者能力的侵蚀。
• LLMs在生成和维护复杂代码项目中的可行性：有观点认为LLMs更适合一次性任务或简单任务，而在复杂项目中表现不佳。

44443109.article_content:
← Back to Blog
Why I'm Dialing Back My LLM Usage
Alberto Fortin
From the
Agentic Engineering Sessions
|
Aired on
July 1st, 2025
We invited
Alberto Fortin
, a seasoned software engineer with 15 years of experience, to share his candid journey with AI. Alberto initially embraced LLMs with genuine enthusiasm, hoping they would revolutionize his development workflow. However, after encountering significant challenges while rebuilding his infrastructure with Go and ClickHouse, he wrote a
thoughtful blog post
reflecting on the gap between AI hype and reality.
For this conversation, Alberto also prepared a
detailed follow-up analysis
testing newer models like Claude Opus 4, examining whether recent improvements have addressed the core issues he encountered.
His experience provides practical lessons for engineers evaluating LLMs in production environments—balancing realistic expectations with an understanding of where these tools genuinely add value versus where they still fall short.
You can
watch the session on YouTube
or read below for some selected quotes.
The Reality Check: When AI Hype Meets Production Code
"I was really shocked at the poor quality of some things, and it was not just about bugs and features not working. I think as a developer who wants to maintain this codebase for the next few years, I also care about it being neat enough."
"I feel like I'm a week away from fixing this, but actually a new small error would come up and then that will take another two weeks to fix."
"I will give my error output to the LLM and then it will spit out something new that will kind of fix it, but also make things a bit more messed up—and break something else in the process."
The Productivity Illusion
"I think everyone just got a little bit overexcited about it because the first iteration, the first little feature, the first autocomplete is like, 'Oh my God, this is amazing. This is like reading my mind.' So you kind of get duped into it a little bit."
"I think we've gotten to a level where we can do probably 10 times as much coding. So we kind of expect that to happen and we require that from the LLMs, but I think everyone just gets a little bit overexcited about it."
Taking Control: The Mental Shift
"I think this is the biggest difference, like a mental shift... I am the software engineer, the senior software engineer, I am the architect. The LLM is the assistant. The assistant responds to me; I make the plan."
"I lost all my trust in LLMs, so I wouldn't give them a big feature again. I'll do very small things like refactoring or a very small-scoped feature."
"I started fixing the bugs myself. Because as soon as you understand this—you have a hundred percent understanding of your codebase and what everything is doing—it's so much easier and quicker for you to go in and fix something."
Practical Wisdom
"If you are confident enough in your skills—you know, a senior developer—and this is not working for you, there's nothing wrong with you. Just try to do the things that you always did and use AI to leverage your knowledge a little bit."
"We've gone up a level, it's great. But also, let's be mindful we're not there yet at the next level... We are offloading some of the programming work, but we still need to do architectural abstractions and make the decisions for the product."
"Let's just try to calm down all this hype and find a balanced approach towards AI. Use it, because I think it's such an amazing revolution in technology, but we're not there yet."
Learn more about Agentic Engineering
Working toward genuine, quality software in an era where code production is not the constraint anymore. Learn our take about
Agentic Engineering
and catch up with all the sessions where we're joined by experts to further develop this topic.

data.title: Exploiting the IKKO Activebuds "AI powered" earbuds
data.author: ajdude
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者购买并研究一款运行Android系统的无线耳塞式设备的过程。该设备因其集成了ChatGPT和其他AI功能而在TikTok上走红。作者通过ADB方式破解设备，发现其直接与OpenAI的API通信，并包含一个OpenAI的密钥。设备还提供了一些应用程序，如Spotify和游戏，但由于屏幕小，操作不便。在研究过程中，作者提取了设备中的APK文件，发现了加密的API端点和密钥，并成功在一个已root的设备上运行了相关应用。此外，作者还提到设备有不同的模式，如“愤怒的Dan”和“恋爱中的Dan”，这些模式有不同的系统提示。最终，作者对该设备的安全性和功能实现提出了质疑和分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对某公司处理安全漏洞的回应及其引发的广泛讨论

不同观点：
• **对公司回应的肯定**：
  - [memesarecool] 认为该公司在漏洞报告处理上比98%的公司都要好，表现出兴趣并积极解决问题。尽管初期对安全性重视不够，但公司展现了责任感。
  
• **对反常现象的讽刺与担忧**：
  - [psim1] 预测未来将有大量不成熟的AI应用进入市场，呼吁关注网络安全，并暗示现在可能是进入该行业的时机。
  - [mikeve] 讽刺帖子中将运行DOOM游戏列为首要问题，而不是客户数据被盗。
  
• **对公司行为的批评与不信任**：
  - [neya] 和 [wedn3sday] 都提到公司试图通过赞助空YouTube频道来掩盖问题，认为这是不道德的行为。
  - [aidos] 对公司声称“技术团队正在努力解决问题”表示怀疑，质疑其是否真的会 diligently 处理。

• **技术层面的讨论**：
  - [JohnMakin] 指出“decrypt”功能仅解码base64是令人难以置信的错误，并提到很多人对base64的安全性存在误解。
  - [brahyam] 分享了其在保护应用免受类似问题影响方面的经验，并提供了几个开源项目作为例子，同时指出了这些项目在滥用保护机制上的不足，进而介绍了自己的开源SDK项目。

• **幽默与娱乐视角**：
  - [ixtli] 和 [jotalea] 以幽默的口吻评论帖子内容，认为这是有趣的“运行DOOM”相关帖，甚至期待看到更多类似的娱乐内容。
  
• **对安全警告的反思**：
  - [mmaunder] 引用了系统提示中关于禁止讨论中国政治的警告，并结合自身经验反思在安全防护中使用“PEOPLE WILL DIE”这类极端警告的必要性和后果。

• **对标题和内容表达的批评**：
  - [jahsome] 批评有人在标题上做文章，结果却让标题更难理解，暗示这种编辑是多余且无效的。

补充讨论：
- **争议的焦点**在于公司对安全漏洞的处理态度和方法，部分评论赞赏公司的积极回应，另一部分则质疑其真实意图和行为。
- **技术层面的讨论**主要围绕具体漏洞的严重性和技术实现的业余性，以及如何通过开源项目提升安全性。
- **幽默评论**为讨论增添了轻松的氛围，但也有人对标题和内容的表达方式提出批评。

44443919.article_content:
So my journey with these earbuds started after I saw them on
this
Mrwhosetheboss video about pointless tech. This device seems to be also popular on TikTok. My suspicions were confirmed, this runs android. So of course i went ahead and bought them.
245 euros later... and they finally arrived!
Before we dive further into this, unlike with
rabbit
, this issue has been properly reported and patched. This is also my first real blog post/disclosure so feedback is appreciated.
Small overview
I like how they strapped a USB-c cable to the outside of the box while there is also a smaller one inside the box. They ran out of box space it seems...
I also wonder if they are legally allowed to use this OpenAI logo (probably not lol)
Anyways, we aren't here for fancy boxes, lets get to the main point. The device itself boots up to a screen with the time and ChatGPT front and center.
There are some other AI features available too like translations. But this isn't a review of the device, you can watch
other YouTube videos
about that. The ChatGPT animation looks way too similar to the actual app and OpenAI could probably get them in legal trouble for stealing their brand identity. I will also mention that the audio quality is absolute shit if you use their EQ profiles but can be upped to a usable level by tweaking the EQ curves yourself.
There are also some apps available in the IKKO store, the reason that there is no google play store available is because these apps are modified specifically for the screen on the ActiveBuds, at least, that is what the CEO says about them. We will check that out in a bit. These apps include some music apps like Spotify, but also some gaming apps like, oh god, SUBWAY SURFERS BAYBEEEEE
Of course all of them unbearable to navigate due to the small screen. However we can now confirm that it most definitely runs android.
Time for some hacking
There is sadly no browser available to directly download other apps. And while you can open the native android settings app, clicking the build number 7 times does not enable developer mode. So i couldn't enable adb it seems. Is it locked that well? heh nope.
Let's just plug it into a pc and see what happens....
What the fuck, they left ADB enabled. Well, this makes it a lot easier.
After sideloading the obligatory DOOM, i began checking out how the ChatGPT integration works on the backend. I first started HTTP inspecting the device, however since i couldn't enable the proper system certificates without rooting the device, i couldn't see exactly to what URL it communicated. Fortunately that wasn't really needed.
Holy shit, holy shit, holy shit, it communicates DIRECTLY TO OPENAI. This means that a ChatGPT key must be present on the device!
I know that this device can be rooted to get the proper certificates installed because
a tool
exists on all Spreadtrum/Unisoc devices which can be used to unlock the bootloader as long as companies use the default signing keys. This was indeed the case here too. However, i couldn't get past the confirmation screen as the device does not have a volume up key to confirm the unlock. I think you are able to sign your own partitions to make it flash them without an unlocked bootloader but that's a bit too advanced for my own liking.
So, i went back to the drawing board and just dumped all of the apps from it with an APK extractor tool. After popping the launcher app into JADX, things immediately became concerning.
The device can communicate to either of these domains.
api.openai.com
Obvious, the OpenAI API
chat1.chat.iamjoy.cn
Seems to be the API for the entire device, including features not related to ChatGPT like the app store. Loading it up in a browser gives a login page.
chat2.chat.iamjoy.cn
Same thing as chat1, possibly a backup server?
openspeech.bytedance.com
No idea, might be a speech recogniser backup instead of whisper, haven't seen communication to this from the device.
www.airdimple.cn
Seems like an OpenAI API mirror or proxy?
Knowing this i went hunting for api endpoints and keys. I found a file called SecurityStringsAPI which contained encrypted endpoints and authentication keys.
You might think, hey that's just base64 idiot, the most basic encoding known to mankind. And well, yeah, it is.
However, there is a second stage which is handled by a native library which is obfuscated to hell. I am not going to even try to read that. Fortunately i didn't have to. I just sideloaded the app on a different device which was rooted, and well,
just like the rabbit apk
, it just works!
Inspecting this device:
Yup, that's an OpenAI key.
Now, while having this access, we can also expose their (pretty funny) system prompt.
The device also has another few modes, which are Angry Dan and In-Love Dan. For the angry one you need to confirm you are 18+ because it actually swears a lot.
The system prompts for these are a bit more boring.
I also noticed that it logs the chat to another endpoint on the chat1 domain. This is probably just

本文讨论了Azure角色权限过度授予和API漏洞带来的安全风险。安全研究人员发现，一些Azure内置角色被错误配置为权限过度宽泛，授予了超出预期的权限。此外，Azure API存在一个漏洞，可能导致VPN密钥泄露。这两者结合形成了一条新的攻击链，使低权限用户能够访问内部云资源和本地网络。

文章首先介绍了Azure RBAC（基于角色的访问控制）的基本概念，包括安全主体、角色定义和权限范围。Azure提供超过400个内置角色，分为通用角色和服务特定角色。通用角色易于管理但权限较宽，而服务特定角色更安全但需要更细致的管理。

研究揭示了一些角色如“Reader”和“Workbook Reader”的权限定义相对合理，但“Managed Applications Reader”等角色可能被不当利用，导致潜在安全风险。

为防范这些威胁，组织应仔细审查角色权限分配，采用最小权限原则，并及时更新安全策略。

Azure's Role Roulette: How Over-Privileged Roles and API Vulnerabilities Expose Enterprise Networks
Ariel Simon
Security Researcher
No items found.
TL;DR
Token Security researchers have discovered several Azure built-in roles that are misconfigured to be over-privileged - they grant more permissions than intended by Azure.
In addition, we discovered another vulnerability in the Azure API that allows attackers to
leak VPN keys
.
Combined, these two issues create a new attack chain that lets a
weak user gain access to both internal cloud assets and on-premises networks.
In this report, we detail the research process that led to the discoveries, their implications, and what organizations can do to stay safe against these threats and other identity-driven attacks.
What is Azure RBAC?
Before jumping in, letâs discuss some basics.
Azureâs permissions model, Azure RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), is, as the name states, based on roles.
Roles are basically groups of permissions that can be assigned to principals (users, service principals, groups, etc). When granting a role to a principal, you create a
role assignment
.
â
Every
role assignment
contains three main components:
Security Principal
- Who is given the permissions?
Role Definition
- Which role is assigned? What permissions does it grant? This section states the name of the role and the
Actions
and
Not Actions
(allow or deny) that this role is granting.
Scope
- What resources is the principal given access to? The scope can be vast, such as an entire management group or subscription, or more specific, like a resource group or a single resource (e.g., a specific VM or storage account).
Role assignment
Azure roles
In Azure, there are more than 400 built-in roles, which can be divided into 2 categories:
Generic
- Roles that grant permissions that apply across all resources and all Azure services in the given scope (e.g.,
Contributor
,
Owner
,
Reader
,
etc.
)
Service-specific
- Roles that grant permissions for a specific service or function in the given scope (e.g.,
Storage Blob Data Reader
or
Virtual Machine Contributor
).
If you assign the
Contributor
role over a subscription scope, it will grant permissions to perform actions over all of the resources in this subscription, regardless if theyâre storage accounts, virtual machines, or any other resource. But if you assign the
Virtual Machine Contributor
, it will grant these permissions only to perform actions over virtual machines in the subscription.
So we can see the tradeoff here: using service-specific roles is the more secure approach, since you are granting fewer permissions, but the generic roles are easier to use since you need to manage fewer roles assignments.
The Problem
Letâs take a look at few roles and their permissions. See if you can tell where things go wrong.
The Reader role
One of Azureâs built-in roles, called
Reader,
is a generic role. As youâd expect, it gives read-only permissions over the resources in the chosen scope. Letâs examine its
role definition
:
{
"assignableScopes": [
"/"
],
"description": "View all resources, but does not allow you to make any changes.",
"id": "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7",
"name": "acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7",
"permissions": [
{
"actions": [
"*/read"
],
"notActions": [],
"dataActions": [],
"notDataActions": []
}
],
"roleName": "Reader",
"roleType": "BuiltInRole",
"type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions"
}
Reader role definition
As we can see in the
actions
property, the permission given is
*/read
, which means it lets you perform any read action in the given scope.
*Note that this does not include data actions (reading data objects like files in storage accounts, key vault secrets, etc). Those require different, service-specific sensitive permissions.
Okay, so a generic role giving generic read permissions, that makes sense.
What about the permissions of service-specific roles?
Workbook Reader
{
"assignableScopes": [
"/"
],
"description": "Can read workbooks.",
"id": "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/b279062a-9be3-42a0-92ae-8b3cf002ec4d",
"name": "b279062a-9be3-42a0-92ae-8b3cf002ec4d",
"permissions": [
{
"actions": [
"microsoft.insights/workbooks/read",
"microsoft.insights/workbooks/revisions/read",
"microsoft.insights/workbooktemplates/read"
],
"notActions": [],
"dataActions": [],
"notDataActions": []
}
],
"roleName": "Workbook Reader",
"roleType": "BuiltInRole",
"type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions"
}
Workbook Reader role definition
If we analyze the
actions
property, we can see that as the description states, it grants read permissions to a few workbook-related objects. So a service-specific role that grants access to a specific service! So far so good.

Managed Applications Reader

âLets you read resources in a managed app

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare的自动调整robots.txt功能及其对AI爬虫和网站流量的影响

不同观点：
• [jasonthorsness] 提到该功能会自动调整robots.txt，但不清楚具体还做了什么，表达了对功能透明度的关注。
• [Meekro] 认为使用Cloudflare的基本缓存配置应能处理爬虫流量，不理解为何人们对此感到困扰，尤其是考虑到当前带宽和CPU成本较低。
• [postalcoder] 指出该功能会阻止遵守robots.txt的透明AI爬虫，这可能反而激励这些爬虫隐藏自己。同时也引用链接说明隐藏行为并不有效。
• [dirkc] 怀疑通过阻止爬虫是否能有效保护原创内容不被用于LLM训练，认为内容最终可能会进入某些LLM的训练集。
• [NullCascade] 提出相反的问题，如何优化内容使其更可能被AI爬虫抓取，指出传统SEO可能不够。
• [btown] 指出该功能是选择性加入的，而非默认开启，同时提到Cloudflare的权力问题。
• [blakesterz] 提到目前被阻止的爬虫列表很短。
• [Sol-] 质疑主要AI公司是否真正遵守robots.txt，怀疑他们有隐藏的爬取行为。
• [account42] 担心此功能会导致普通用户遇到更多CAPTCHA验证。
• [dawnerd] 分享了个人经验，表示该功能有效减少了服务器负载，特别提到了对微软和Meta流量的阻止效果。
• [alganet] 认为AI自由使用网站数据会导致人们失去创造数字内容的动力，预测AI会最终摧毁网络。
• [badlibrarian] 询问是否修复了自动阻止RSS feed的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Cloudflare功能的实际效果、透明度、以及对AI公司遵守规则的信任问题。
• 有人关注该功能对普通用户体验的影响，如[account42]提到的CAPTCHA问题。
• 讨论中还提到了具体技术实现和配置细节，如[dawnerd]分享的实际配置经验和效果。
• 链接和引用提供了额外的背景信息和深入讨论，如[postalcoder]和[cmg]提供的链接。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于该功能是否有效保护网站内容以及其对不同类型流量的处理方式，特别是对AI爬虫的阻止是否会产生反效果，以及对普通用户体验的影响。

data.title: Private sector lost 33k jobs, badly missing expectations of 100k increase
data.author: ceejayoz
data.article_summary: 2023年6月，私营部门招聘意外收缩，ADP报告显示私营部门减少了33,000个工作岗位，为2023年3月以来首次下降。经济学家此前预计增加100,000个岗位。服务业岗位受创最重，专业/商业服务和医疗/教育领域分别减少了56,000和52,000个岗位。尽管制造业和采矿业岗位增加，整体服务岗位减少了66,000个。中西部和西部地区就业收缩最严重，而南部地区岗位增加。小型企业岗位流失最多，而拥有超过500名员工的大型企业岗位增长最多。工资增长略有放缓，S&P 500指数今年上涨超过4%。经济不确定性增加，投资者正密切关注即将发布的政府就业报告。
